{
  "content": "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Content module: Parts V, VI, VII and Appendix A."""

TECH_INTRO = [
 ("h1", "V.  WITNESS GROUP B — MERIDIAN TECHNICAL TEAM"),
 ("p", "The technical-team witnesses are the only source in this matter that can convert PathForge's "
       "published self-description into a module-by-module, contributor-by-contributor, artifact-by-artifact "
       "record, and their materials — repositories and commit history, dependency and license manifests, "
       "test harnesses and raw test data, build and release records — will either substantiate or undercut "
       "the independent-development position stated in Meridian's April 5, 2024 letter and in white paper "
       "Section 7.2. Because the white paper attributes the work collectively to \"the PathForge "
       "Engineering Team\" and to \"a dedicated engineering team of approximately 45 working full-time on "
       "PathForge development and customer integration,\" individual testimony is required to establish who "
       "actually did what, and which engineers can speak to the April 2018 through September 2020 period at "
       "all."),
 ("p", "This group should be interviewed after Holt's first session and before the legal lead, for the "
       "reasons given in Part VII: their knowledge is predominantly technical fact, so the interview can "
       "proceed at full depth without the privilege bifurcation Part VI requires and without the "
       "conflict-of-interest assessment Part III.D requires for Holt; and their artifacts are the most "
       "perishable material in the case, since repository migrations, decommissioned shares, and departed "
       "contractors permanently degrade them."),
 ("p", "Interview format: one session per witness, sequenced so that module owners for the four modules "
       "named in white paper Section 7.1 are covered first, followed by release and test engineering, then "
       "infrastructure and DevOps custodians, then whoever owns build and open-source compliance. Each "
       "session should open with the witness's own role and period of involvement before any document is "
       "shown. Witnesses should not be shown Exhibit F; it is a SkyVault-side record of a SkyVault account "
       "and its relevance to a Meridian engineer is limited to the questions it raises about inbound "
       "material."),

TECH = [
 ("T-1",
  "Which PathForge modules have you personally worked on, during what periods, and what did you write "
  "yourself as opposed to reviewing, integrating, or maintaining?",
  "White Paper Sec. 1 (\"a dedicated engineering team of approximately 45 working full-time on PathForge "
  "development and customer integration\"; \"The company employs 112 people\"), Sec. 7.1 items 1-4 "
  "(Navigation Module; Swarm Coordination Module; Analytics Dashboard; Hardware Integration Layer), Sec. "
  "5.4 closing paragraph (each module \"was developed as an independent engineering effort within the "
  "broader PathForge program\"), Sec. 7.2 timeline bullets (module-specific date ranges). Complaint para. "
  "57 (attributing the paper to \"Dr. Marcus Holt and the Meridian engineering team\"), para. 12 (\"Meridian "
  "employs approximately 112 people,\" on information and belief).",
  "Converts the white paper's collective attribution into identifiable percipient witnesses and custodians, "
  "which is a prerequisite for authentication, for deposition planning, and for testing whether the "
  "\"approximately 45\" engineers claimed in Sec. 1 can be matched to actual contributor records. It also "
  "establishes who, if anyone, was present during the April 2018 to September 2020 window on which "
  "Complaint para. 54's timeline inference depends — a window that a later-joining engineer cannot speak "
  "to at all."),

 ("T-2",
  "For the module you own, describe the repository layout, the earliest commit you can locate, the "
  "branching and merge history, and every repository move, platform migration, rewrite, squash, or "
  "force-push that has occurred since 2018.",
  "Complaint para. 61(iii) (demand for \"a full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories to "
  "determine the extent of Meridian's misappropriation and infringement\"), para. 119 (alleging Holt "
  "\"copied, modified, and/or incorporated substantial portions of that code into Meridian's PathForge "
  "firmware\"), para. 120 (alleging \"direct copies, modified versions, and/or derivative works of "
  "SkyVault's copyrighted AeroCore source code\"), para. 118 (alleging PathForge firmware \"contains code "
  "that is substantially similar\"). Response Letter item 3 (declining repository access as \"premature, "
  "overbroad, and without legal basis outside of formal litigation with appropriate protective measures in "
  "place\"). White Paper Sec. 7.2 bullets \"April 2018\" and \"Q3 2018 - Q4 2019\".",
  "Repository history is the primary evidence for and against the copyright and trade-secret use "
  "allegations, and it is the material Meridian has so far declined to expose to a third-party audit. "
  "Establishing now whether an unbroken, credible history exists — and in particular whether early history "
  "was lost to a migration, a squash, or a rewrite — determines whether the independent-development "
  "position asserted in the April 5 letter is provable in discovery. A gap or a rewrite is itself a fact "
  "the matter team must know before that representation is repeated in an answer or a discovery response."),

 ("T-3",
  "List every third-party library, framework, SDK, toolchain, dataset, model, or open-source component "
  "your module depends on, and show me where each is declared, where its license text is stored, and where "
  "any attribution or notice is recorded.",
  "White Paper Sec. 4.2 (DroneNav's \"publicly available codebase implemented the core pipeline of "
  "feature tracking, sliding-window optimization, keyframe management, and IMU pre-integration\"), Sec. "
  "7.2 bullets \"Q3 2018 - Q4 2019,\" \"Q1 2019 - Q3 2020\" and \"Q2 2019 - Q1 2021\" (each attributing "
  "design influence to published literature or public implementations), References items 1-4, Sec. 3.1 "
  "(sensor suite: LiDAR 20 Hz and 120 m range; stereo 30 fps and 0.5-30 m; 6-axis IMU 200 Hz; ultrasonic "
  "0-5 m at 40 Hz), Sec. 5.2 (\"dedicated radio link operating on 900 MHz or 2.4 GHz frequency bands\"; "
  "\"custom lightweight message protocol\"). Response Letter para. 3 (\"robust internal compliance "
  "processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property\"). "
  "ECIAA Exhibit A Table Row 2 (MIT-licensed RoboNav toolkit).",
  "Dependency manifests are the objective test of whether any third-party code entered PathForge — "
  "including DroneNav code, anything descending from Holt's two disclosed prior inventions, or anything "
  "traceable to SkyVault. They also test the compliance representation already made in writing to opposing "
  "counsel: if no bill of materials, license scan, or attribution record exists, that representation lacks "
  "a documented foundation and must not be repeated without qualification. The hardware and radio "
  "specifications in Sec. 3.1 and Sec. 5.2 additionally identify vendor SDKs whose presence would be "
  "expected and whose absence would be informative."),

 ("T-4",
  "Has any file, folder, commit, dependency, or binary in your module ever been identified internally as "
  "originating from SkyVault, from Dr. Holt's pre-Meridian work, or from an unidentified external source? "
  "Has any similarity scan or provenance review ever been run, by whom, and what did it produce?",
  "Complaint paras. 33, 116 and 118 (naming the AeroCore source files \"navfusion.c,\" \"pathoptengine.h,\" "
  "and \"swarm_proto.cpp\" as the copyrighted works and alleging substantial similarity to them), paras. "
  "119-120. Exhibit F, \"Forensic Log\" Row # 34 Notes (the transfer \"spanned\" five named Confluence "
  "spaces) — and the absence from Rows # 1 through # 50 of any reference to AeroCore or to any of those "
  "three file names, which \"Report Metadata\" cell B8 explains by the exclusion of code repositories from "
  "the data sources. ECIAA Exhibit A Rows 1-2 and Sec. 5.3. White Paper Sec. 7.2 closing paragraph.",
  "Tests the copyright count at file level. None of the three source files SkyVault names at Complaint "
  "paras. 33, 116 and 118 appears anywhere in the 50 rows of Exhibit F, and the white-paper excerpt never "
  "mentions AeroCore, so the connection between the pleaded files and anything in PathForge presently "
  "rests on pleading alone. The answer establishes whether Meridian has ever run its own comparison — a "
  "fact with consequences for privilege, for the April 5 representations, and for how Question L-7 must "
  "be framed."),

 ("T-5",
  "Describe how your module is built, tested, and released: the test harnesses, the flight-test campaigns, "
  "the methodology behind each published benchmark figure, the version milestones, and where the raw "
  "results are stored.",
  "White Paper Sec. 3.3 and its table (obstacle detection rate 99.7%; false positive rate under 0.2%; "
  "average detection-to-avoidance latency 38 ms; 8 cm RMS structured and 14 cm RMS unstructured) plus the "
  "comparison text (Vasquez (2016) \"47 milliseconds detection latency and 15 centimeters positional "
  "accuracy\"; \"a 19% improvement in detection latency and a 47% improvement in positional accuracy in "
  "structured environments\"), Sec. 4.4 and its table (drift under 0.5%; 45 minutes maximum GPS-denied "
  "endurance; 97.3% mission completion) and its named test environments (10,000 sq. ft. warehouse; "
  "1.2-kilometer utility tunnel; simulated urban canyon with 8-15 m building separations), Sec. 5.4 and "
  "its table (24 drones maximum tested; 14 ms average inter-drone latency; zero collisions across 1,200+ "
  "hours; sub-linear scaling), Sec. 3.2 Steps 1-7, Sec. 5.3 (default 3 m safety margin; deconfliction "
  "\"within one planning cycle (typically under 100 milliseconds from conflict detection to maneuver "
  "initiation)\"). Complaint para. 68 (dependent claims 3, 7 and 12).",
  "Timestamped test and release artifacts are the most persuasive independent-development evidence "
  "available, because they were generated in the ordinary course without reference to SkyVault, and they "
  "simultaneously verify or falsify the published figures the complaint relies on through Complaint para. "
  "58 and the para. 67 claim chart. They are also the only supplied route to the three features mapped to "
  "'561 dependent claims 3, 7 and 12, none of which appears in the white-paper excerpt. Raw harness "
  "output additionally establishes test-environment provenance, which bears on whether the benchmarks are "
  "reproducible at all."),

 ("T-6",
  "Do the features SkyVault describes — a \"configurable threat parameter interface,\" \"multi-resolution "
  "environmental mapping,\" and a \"fail-safe autonomous return-to-home function\" — exist in PathForge? "
  "If so, where, since which version, and who built them? If not, what is the closest functionality in the "
  "product?",
  "Complaint para. 68 (all three features, said to meet dependent claims 3, 7 and 12 of the '561 Patent), "
  "para. 67 claim chart row 1[c] (\"Threat Assessment Module\" applying \"operator-configurable threat "
  "parameters, including proximity thresholds, velocity vectors, and object classification rules,\" "
  "quoted to \"Section 4.1\") and row 1[d] (\"Dynamic Path Replanner\" generating \"optimal alternative "
  "trajectories in under 50 milliseconds upon obstacle detection,\" quoted to \"Section 4.3\"). White "
  "Paper Sec. 3.2 Step 6 (\"Detected obstacles are classified as static or dynamic based on temporal "
  "consistency analysis across successive occupancy grid updates\"; velocity vectors estimated \"using a "
  "multi-frame tracking algorithm\"), Step 7 (\"a rapid replanning algorithm generates an avoidance "
  "maneuver within the UAV's dynamic flight envelope ... optimizes for minimum deviation from the planned "
  "path\"), Sec. 4.3 (adaptive path optimization; battery constraints; \"Obstacle data from the sensor "
  "fusion module (Section 3) is integrated directly into the path planner\"), Sec. 5.3 (priority-based "
  "deconfliction). None of the three quoted terms, and no 50-millisecond replanning figure, appears in the "
  "excerpt.",
  "The excerpt describes functionally adjacent behaviour under different names, which means either the "
  "complete 42-page paper or the shipped product must supply the mapping SkyVault asserts. Establishing "
  "what the product actually does, and when each feature entered, is the factual basis for any position on "
  "Complaint para. 68 — and it must come from engineers and product records, not from the marketing paper. "
  "The answer also feeds Question H-22, since a feature genuinely present in the product but absent from "
  "the excerpt points to a fuller Exhibit G rather than to an inaccurate claim chart."),

 ("T-7",
  "Who at Meridian has ever held or seen a SkyVault document, file, drive, dataset, or product? Separately: "
  "how would such material have entered Meridian's systems in 2018 through 2020 without being detected, "
  "and what controls existed?",
  "Complaint paras. 55, 95, 108, 130 and 136 (Meridian's receipt, knowledge, and reason to know). Exhibit "
  "F, \"Forensic Log\" Row # 34 (destination \"Removable Disk (F:\\SkyVault_Export\\)\"; device identifier "
  "\"USB\\VID_0781&PID_5581\\4C530001221029118035 (SanDisk Ultra 128GB)\"), Row # 46 (\"Employee declined "
  "to return or identify USB device\"). ECIAA Sec. 3.5 (return and deletion obligations), Sec. 2.4 "
  "(\"Company Materials\"). Response Letter para. 3 (denial).",
  "Addresses the derivative-liability theory at Complaint para. 130 from both directions. The second half "
  "of the question is as important as the first: the absence of any detection is meaningful only if the "
  "engineers can describe the ingestion controls that existed at the time — endpoint management, "
  "removable-media policy, inbound-file scanning, repository import review — and none of that is "
  "documented in any supplied file. If no such controls existed, that is a fact the matter team must know "
  "before the April 5 compliance representation is repeated."),

 ("T-8",
  "What were Meridian's engineering onboarding controls in 2018 concerning prior-employer materials — IP "
  "questionnaires, prior-restriction attestations, clean-room instructions, device imaging, or repository "
  "access reviews? Do records of them exist for Dr. Holt and for each early engineer?",
  "Response Letter para. 3 (\"Meridian maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to "
  "safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property. SkyVault's allegations to "
  "the contrary are without merit.\"). Complaint paras. 95 and 108 (\"with knowledge or reason to know\"), "
  "para. 130 (Meridian \"knowingly received, accepted, and exploited\"; \"was aware of Holt's obligations "
  "under the ECIAA and induced, participated in, and benefited from Holt's breach\"), para. 136 (\"aware, "
  "or should have been aware\"). ECIAA Sec. 3.5(c) (the written-certification mechanism as a comparator "
  "for what an onboarding control could capture) and Sec. 5.3 with Exhibit A (the prior-invention "
  "disclosure mechanism as a comparator).",
  "This is the factual predicate for a representation already made in writing to opposing counsel. If "
  "onboarding attestations, IP questionnaires, or clean-team instructions exist, they are strong evidence "
  "against Complaint paras. 130 and 136; if they do not, the April 5, 2024 statement is unsupported and "
  "must be corrected or carefully qualified before it is repeated in an answer or a discovery response. "
  "Either outcome is a fact to be collected, and neither may be assumed."),

 ("T-9",
  "Describe every system, device, share, backup, archive, and personal account where PathForge development "
  "records live today, including anything migrated, decommissioned, or held by a former employee, "
  "contractor, or vendor.",
  "Complaint para. 61(iii) (source-code forensic audit demand), para. 125 and Prayer para. 17 (impoundment "
  "and, upon final judgment, destruction of all infringing copies under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 503). Response "
  "Letter item 3. Exhibit F, \"Report Metadata\" cells B7, B8 and B13 — illustrating how a "
  "custodian-scoped and source-scoped review can leave an entire class of systems outside the examined "
  "population, and how a selected extract can present itself as a review of \"[a]ll\" events while "
  "covering 50 of 12,847.",
  "Builds the custodian and source map needed for a defensible hold and production, and for assessing "
  "whether Meridian could itself be exposed to an incomplete-collection challenge. Exhibit F is the "
  "cautionary template rather than the model: Meridian must be able to state with the same precision what "
  "its own review will and will not cover, and must avoid producing an extract that discloses its own "
  "selection criteria only in a metadata note. Prayer para. 17 makes the location of every PathForge copy "
  "a live issue independent of discovery."),

 ("T-10",
  "Was any PathForge design, prototype, simulation, or documentation created before April 11, 2018, or "
  "between February 16 and April 11, 2018? Where would such material be, and who would have it?",
  "White Paper Sec. 7.2 bullet \"April 2018\" (\"Meridian Dynamics, Inc. incorporated in Delaware. "
  "PathForge development begins under Dr. Marcus Holt's technical leadership\"), Sec. 1 (\"Developed from "
  "the ground up beginning in 2018\"), Sec. 2 (\"When Meridian Dynamics began development of PathForge in "
  "2018\"). Complaint paras. 9 and 53 (formation \"on or about April 11, 2018\"; \"[a]pproximately two "
  "months after his departure\"), para. 54 (timeline inference). ECIAA Sec. 3.2(a) (perpetual "
  "trade-secret obligation), Sec. 3.4 (residual skills and publicly available information).",
  "Tests the two-month-gap inference at Complaint para. 54 against artifacts rather than assertion. If "
  "design material predates incorporation, that fact must be located, dated and provenance-checked — it "
  "may support independent development, or it may create a new problem if it post-dates February 16, 2018 "
  "and draws on SkyVault sources. The engineers are the only source for this, and the answer must not be "
  "assumed in either direction. Early artifacts held on personal accounts or pre-Meridian hardware are the "
  "most likely to have been lost, which is why this question is asked early."),

 ("T-11",
  "Who at Meridian contributed technical content to the July 2022 white paper, who reviewed it, and can you "
  "identify the source documents or data behind each figure and each section you contributed? Who holds the "
  "complete 42-page version, including Section 6 and the appendices?",
  "White Paper P0003 (cover attribution \"Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder / PathForge Engineering "
  "Team\"), P0005 (\"Public Release / Marketing Technical Paper\"), P0006 (\"This document is an excerpt "
  "of the full PathForge Technical White Paper (42 pages). This excerpt contains Sections 1-5 and Section "
  "7, omitting detailed hardware specifications (Section 6) and appendices.\"), the Sec. 6 placeholder "
  "(\"[Section 6 — Hardware Integration Specifications — omitted from this excerpt. The full white paper "
  "contains detailed specifications for PathForge's hardware abstraction layer, supported sensor hardware "
  "models, and drone platform integration guides.]\"), Sec. 3.3, Sec. 4.4 and Sec. 5.4 tables, References "
  "items 1-4. Complaint paras. 57-58, 67, 77 and 85 (reliance on the paper as Exhibit G), Exhibit List "
  "entry \"Exhibit G,\" paras. 38(e), 91(e) and 105(e) (TS-5, \"[h]ardware integration specifications for "
  "LiDAR sensor arrays\").",
  "Identifies the percipient authors behind each published statement and the underlying data, which is "
  "necessary both to authenticate the paper's contents and to determine whether the benchmark tables and "
  "the provenance statements were supported by records when published. Section 6 is singled out because it "
  "is the omitted portion of Meridian's own publication that maps most directly onto TS-5 as pleaded at "
  "Complaint paras. 38(e), 91(e) and 105(e) — Meridian may already have publicly disclosed the very "
  "category SkyVault claims as secret, or Section 6 may be innocuous, and only the complete paper will "
  "show which."),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Part VI
LEGAL_INTRO = [
 ("h1", "VI.  WITNESS GROUP C — MERIDIAN'S LEGAL LEAD"),
 ("p", "The legal lead is identified in the supplied materials as Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian "
       "Dynamics, Inc. — the only in-house Meridian person named in the package, appearing in the cc line "
       "of the April 5, 2024 Brackwell & Haines response. He is the witness who can establish the "
       "discoverable facts of the pre-suit correspondence chain, the preservation programme, and the "
       "compliance processes that Meridian has already asserted in writing to opposing counsel. Because a "
       "cc line is a thin basis for assuming either role or knowledge, Question L-1 confirms title, tenure, "
       "and responsibility before anything else is asked."),
 ("p", "This interview must be deliberately bifurcated. Dates, recipients, routing, distribution lists, "
       "hold notices, custodian identities, what was gathered and transmitted, and which policies exist and "
       "what they produced are ordinary fact events and are asked directly. The content of advice from "
       "Brackwell & Haines or from in-house counsel, the mental impressions formed about the strength of "
       "SkyVault's claims, the reasoning behind the positions taken in the April 5 letter, the assessment "
       "of any limitations or validity defence, and the substance of any settlement discussion are likely "
       "protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work-product doctrine and are not asked. Where a "
       "witness volunteers protected material, the interviewer should note the topic, stop, and log it "
       "rather than develop it."),
 ("p", "A further caution: this witness is both a fact witness and a likely privilege holder, and the "
       "interview record may itself become the subject of a privilege dispute. The session should be "
       "documented as fact-gathering, questions should be phrased to elicit events rather than "
       "assessments, and the interviewer should record contemporaneously where a protected topic was "
       "reached and declined so that the boundary is visible on the face of the record."),
]

LEGAL = [
 ("L-1",
  "Please confirm your title, your tenure at Meridian, and your responsibility scope; and identify everyone "
  "else in Meridian's legal function who has touched the SkyVault matter at any time.",
  "Response Letter P0025 (cc line: \"Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc. (via email)\"), "
  "P0003 and P0022 (Laura Brackwell, Partner, Brackwell & Haines LLP, the signing attorney), P0006 "
  "(addressee Theresa N. Voss, Partner, Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP). Complaint para. 62 (\"Meridian's "
  "outside counsel, Brackwell & Haines LLP, responded to SkyVault's cease-and-desist letter by letter\"); "
  "signature block \"Theresa N. Voss, Texas Bar No. 24078133\" and certificate of service dated October 2, "
  "2024.",
  "The supplied record identifies this witness only as a cc recipient, so his authority, tenure, and actual "
  "role must be established before his knowledge is treated as Meridian's for any purpose, including "
  "imputation under Complaint paras. 130 and 136. The answer also fixes the privilege population — who sits "
  "inside the legal function and who is a business custodian — which determines the scope of any later "
  "privilege log and whether business-side recipients of advice fall outside protection."),

 ("L-2",
  "Describe how the March 12, 2024 letter reached Meridian, who received it, on what date, in what form, "
  "and what was done with it in the ordinary course.",
  "Complaint para. 61 (letter sent March 12, 2024 by Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP \"addressed to Priya "
  "Chandrasekaran, CEO, at Meridian's headquarters in Austin, Texas,\" identifying the '561, '227 and '889 "
  "Patents, describing the trade secret and copyright claims, and demanding (i) cessation of all use, sale "
  "and distribution of PathForge, (ii) $15 million in licensing fees for past infringement, and (iii) \"a "
  "full forensic audit of Meridian's source code repositories\"). Response Letter P0007 (Re line: \"Your "
  "March 12, 2024 Correspondence on Behalf of SkyVault Technologies LLC — Allegations Against Meridian "
  "Dynamics, Inc.\"), P0009 (\"We write to acknowledge receipt of that correspondence\"), P0005 (\"Via "
  "Email and U.S. Certified Mail\").",
  "The March 12, 2024 letter is not among the supplied materials, and its contents are known to us only "
  "through Complaint para. 61 and through the matters the April 5 response addresses; nothing beyond those "
  "two sources may be attributed to it. Receipt date, routing, and distribution are plain fact events that "
  "fix the notice date underpinning the willfulness allegations at Complaint para. 63 and paras. 69-70, 78 "
  "and 86, and that determine when Meridian's own preservation duty arose. The letter must be located and "
  "collected, together with its envelope or delivery receipt if it came by certified mail."),

 ("L-3",
  "What documents, information, and personnel did Meridian supply to Brackwell & Haines before the April 5, "
  "2024 response was sent? Please describe only what was gathered and transmitted, and who gathered it — "
  "not any advice you or Meridian received, and not the reasoning behind any position taken.",
  "Response Letter P0010 (\"Meridian has reviewed the three United States patents identified in your "
  "letter ... Your letter does not provide any claim-by-claim analysis or other substantive basis to "
  "support SkyVault's assertions of infringement, and we are aware of none.\"), P0011 (\"Meridian "
  "independently developed its PathForge platform through the efforts of its engineering teams and "
  "respects the intellectual property rights of others. Meridian maintains robust internal compliance "
  "processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property.\"), "
  "P0012-P0015 (the three itemised refusals), P0025 (cc to Kessler). Complaint para. 62.",
  "Every factual assertion in the April 5 letter — that Meridian \"reviewed\" the patents, that it is "
  "\"aware of\" no claim-by-claim analysis, that development was independent, and that \"robust internal "
  "compliance processes\" exist — implies an underlying investigation whose inputs are discoverable facts "
  "even though counsel's conclusions are not. Identifying who was asked, what was gathered, and what exists "
  "in writing tells us whether those representations have a documentary foundation and which custodians hold "
  "it. The question is bounded on its face to collection and transmission so that the record shows the "
  "privilege boundary was observed; if the answer moves toward what counsel advised or concluded, the "
  "interviewer notes the topic and stops."),

 ("L-4",
  "What specific compliance processes did Meridian have in place on April 5, 2024 and before, to guard "
  "against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property? Where are the policies, training "
  "records, attestations, review outputs, and any code-scanning results?",
  "Response Letter P0011 (the \"robust internal compliance processes\" representation and the statement "
  "that \"SkyVault's allegations to the contrary are without merit\"), P0016 (reservation of \"defenses of "
  "non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, independent development\"). Complaint paras. 95 and 108 "
  "(\"knowledge or reason to know\"), para. 130 (\"knowingly received, accepted, and exploited\"; \"aware of "
  "Holt's obligations under the ECIAA\"; \"induced, participated in, and benefited from\"), para. 136 "
  "(\"aware, or should have been aware\"). ECIAA Sec. 5.3 and Exhibit A (the prior-invention disclosure "
  "mechanism as a comparator for what an onboarding control could have captured).",
  "This representation has already been made in writing to opposing counsel and will be treated as a party "
  "statement, so its factual basis must exist or the letter must be corrected. The question is directed at "
  "artifacts — written policies, IP onboarding questionnaires, open-source review records, code-scanning "
  "output, training completion records — because Count VII's derivative theory at Complaint para. 130 and "
  "the unjust-enrichment knowledge allegation at para. 136 are most efficiently met with contemporaneous "
  "process evidence. The absence of artifacts is itself a material finding that must surface before an "
  "answer is filed, not after."),

 ("L-5",
  "When did Meridian learn that Dr. Holt had signed a confidentiality and invention-assignment agreement "
  "with SkyVault? When did Meridian first obtain a copy? What did Meridian do with that knowledge?",
  "ECIAA (executed and effective June 13, 2016; Recitals; Secs. 3.1-3.5, 5.1-5.6, 7.1; Exhibit A with two "
  "listed Prior Inventions and \"Employee Initials: _M.H._\" dated June 13, 2016). Complaint paras. 45-46 "
  "(the ECIAA as Exhibit E and a summary of Secs. 3, 5 and 7), para. 127 (\"On June 13, 2016, Dr. Marcus "
  "Holt entered into the Employee Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement\"), para. 130 (\"On "
  "information and belief, Meridian was aware of Holt's obligations under the ECIAA\"). Response Letter — "
  "silent as to the ECIAA; the April 5, 2024 letter addresses the three patents, the trade secret and "
  "copyright allegations, and the three demands, and does not mention the agreement.",
  "Meridian's exposure on Count VII is derivative of Holt's breach and turns on its knowledge under "
  "Complaint para. 130, yet the only supplied Meridian-side document that would ordinarily address an "
  "employee's prior restrictive covenants says nothing about the ECIAA. Establishing when Meridian knew, "
  "whether Holt disclosed the agreement or produced a copy at onboarding in 2018, and what was done is a "
  "pure fact question with significant consequences. It also identifies whether the executed original now "
  "in the package came from Meridian's own files or from SkyVault's production — a custody point that "
  "affects how we may use it."),

 ("L-6",
  "What preservation steps did Meridian take, and on what dates, after the March 12, 2024 letter, after the "
  "October 2, 2024 filing, and at any earlier point in this dispute? Who issued the notices, to whom, and "
  "what was collected?",
  "Complaint signature block \"Date: October 2, 2024,\" certificate of service (\"on October 2, 2024, the "
  "foregoing ... was filed electronically via the Court's CM/ECF system\"), caption (\"Civil Action No. "
  "2:24-cv-00817-JRG\"), para. 61 (March 12, 2024 letter), Prayer paras. 8 and 17 (permanent injunction; "
  "impoundment and destruction of all infringing materials under 17 U.S.C. Sec. 503). Exhibit F, \"Report "
  "Metadata\" cell B14 (\"CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION\"), "
  "\"Forensic Log\" Row # 40 (SkyVault's February 12, 2018 note: \"IT to preserve all logs and endpoint "
  "data per litigation hold\"), Rows # 45 and # 49 (forensic image requested; workstation \"secured in IT "
  "evidence storage\"), cell B12 (chain of custody; evidence locker HFG-2018-0034).",
  "Preservation dates, hold notices, custodian lists, and suspension of auto-deletion are discoverable "
  "facts, and the comparison with SkyVault's conduct is instructive: Exhibit F shows SkyVault imposing a "
  "litigation hold, imaging a workstation, and securing hardware in February 2018, roughly six and a half "
  "years before suit. Meridian's corresponding record is absent from the supplied set entirely. Prayer para. "
  "17 makes the location of every PathForge copy a live issue independent of the merits, which raises the "
  "stakes on the completeness of the hold."),

 ("L-7",
  "Has Meridian ever conducted or commissioned any internal review, code scan, provenance analysis, or "
  "comparison of PathForge against SkyVault materials? Who ran it, when, on whose instruction, and what "
  "exists in writing as a result?",
  "Response Letter P0010 (\"Meridian has reviewed the three United States patents identified in your "
  "letter\"; \"we are aware of none\"), P0011 (independent-development and compliance assertions), item 3 "
  "(declining \"any forensic audit or inspection\" of source-code repositories). Complaint para. 61(iii), "
  "para. 119 (alleging \"striking similarities between the AeroCore firmware and the PathForge firmware — "
  "including in structure, sequence, and organization, as well as in specific code implementations\"), "
  "paras. 67, 77 and 85 (claim-chart and white-paper-based mappings). White Paper Sec. 7.2 closing "
  "paragraph.",
  "Distinguishes an ordinary-course factual investigation, whose inputs and underlying data are generally "
  "discoverable, from a review undertaken at counsel's direction in anticipation of litigation, whose "
  "analyses and mental impressions are likely work product. The interviewer must establish whether any "
  "comparison was ever run, by whom, when, and on what instruction, without eliciting the conclusions "
  "counsel reached. The point is practical as well as doctrinal: if a similarity analysis exists and was "
  "circulated to business personnel without a privilege review, protection may already be compromised, and "
  "that must be known now rather than in a motion."),

 ("L-8",
  "Between March 12, 2024 and the October 2, 2024 filing, what communications passed between Meridian and "
  "SkyVault or its counsel? Were any calls or meetings held? Please give existence, dates, participants, "
  "and where the records are — not the substance of any settlement discussion.",
  "Response Letter P0009 (\"without waiver of any rights, claims, or defenses\"; \"Nothing in this letter "
  "constitutes an admission\"), P0016 (reservation of all rights and defences, including fee recovery), "
  "P0017 (\"Meridian remains willing to engage in good-faith discussions ... We would be pleased to arrange "
  "a call or meeting at a mutually convenient time ... This offer is made without prejudice to Meridian's "
  "position as set forth herein ... Any such discussions would need to be conducted on a without-prejudice "
  "basis and subject to applicable rules governing settlement communications.\"), P0018 (request that "
  "SkyVault and its counsel \"refrain from contacting Meridian's officers and employees directly\"; request "
  "that future correspondence carry the reference \"Meridian Dynamics, Inc. — SkyVault IP Matter\"). "
  "Complaint para. 62 (the April 5 response \"categorically refused to comply with any of SkyVault's "
  "demands\"), para. 63 (continued sales after notice).",
  "The correspondence chain is a lead family in its own right, and the interval between the April 5 response "
  "and the October 2 filing is wholly undocumented in the supplied set. Establishing whether any call, "
  "meeting, or further letter occurred is a fact question; the content of settlement negotiations is likely "
  "inadmissible and partly privileged, so the question is confined to existence, dates, participants and "
  "document location. It also tests Complaint para. 63's continued-conduct narrative against Meridian's own "
  "commercial records for that period, and identifies whether SkyVault honoured the P0018 no-contact "
  "request."),

 ("L-9",
  "Has Meridian or its counsel had any contact with Dr. Holt about this matter before today? Has anyone "
  "advised him regarding his personal exposure on Count VII, and has he retained his own counsel?",
  "Complaint paras. 127-132 (Count VII pleaded on Holt's contractual obligations, with Meridian's liability "
  "framed as derivative at para. 130), paras. 94 and 107 (Holt named personally as the actor who "
  "\"downloaded approximately 4,700 files\"), Prayer para. 5 (\"A finding and judgment that Meridian, "
  "through Holt, has breached the Employee Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement\"), para. 2 "
  "(Holt \"co-founded Meridian\"). ECIAA Sec. 8.3 (prevailing-party attorneys' fees \"[i]n any action to "
  "enforce this Agreement\"), Sec. 9.2 (\"Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be "
  "resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Collin County, Texas\") — note the "
  "divergence from the Eastern District of Texas, Marshall Division forum in which the complaint was filed. "
  "Response Letter P0018 (no-contact request to SkyVault).",
  "Holt faces personal contractual exposure while Meridian's liability is pleaded as derivative, so their "
  "interests may diverge — a conflict that must be assessed before any joint interview, before the Upjohn "
  "determination described in Part III.D is made, and before Holt's statements are treated as aligned with "
  "Meridian's. This question establishes the factual state of representation and prior communication. It is "
  "not a request for legal advice, and the interviewer should not explore counsel's assessment of the "
  "conflict. The ECIAA Sec. 9.2 forum clause is flagged because it bears on whether Holt's personal exposure "
  "could be pursued in a different forum from this action, which is a consideration for the conflict "
  "assessment and for Part VII sequencing."),

 ("L-10",
  "Exhibit F is marked as SkyVault's attorney work product prepared in anticipation of litigation, yet it "
  "was filed as a public complaint exhibit, and its own metadata states that 50 events were selected from a "
  "population of 12,847. What has Meridian received, requested, or done about the unselected population, the "
  "file-level detail, and the underlying forensic engagement?",
  "Exhibit F, \"Report Metadata\" cell B13 (\"This extract contains selected events relevant to the bulk "
  "file transfer incident involving user mholt on 02/09/2018. Full audit log contains 12,847 events for the "
  "review period; 50 events selected as relevant to the scope of engagement.\"), cell B14 (work-product "
  "legend), cells B4-B6 (\"Prepared By\" Hargrove Forensics Group; \"Prepared For\" Callister, Voss & "
  "Greenbaum LLP; \"Date of Report\" March 5, 2018), cell B7 (Scope of Review limited to \"All Confluence "
  "workspace and endpoint security events for user account 'mholt' ... January 1, 2018 through February 28, "
  "2018\"), cell B9 (\"Total Events in Scope: 50\"), cell B11 (\"Thomas R. Hargrove, CFCE, EnCE\"), cell "
  "B12 (chain of custody with the truncated hash \"9a3f...d82e\" and locker HFG-2018-0034); \"Forensic Log\" "
  "Rows # 45, # 49 and # 50. Complaint para. 50 (describing Exhibit F as identifying \"the date, time, file "
  "count, and destination device associated with the bulk download event\"), Exhibit List entry \"Exhibit F.\"",
  "Determines what discovery has been sought or received, and frames four concrete, document-anchored lines "
  "on which the Holt and technical interviews depend: (i) the 12,797 unselected events, which are the only "
  "place the 3,174 files and 8,791.2 MB by which Row # 34 exceeds the six logged staging exports could be "
  "accounted for; (ii) the stated review period of January 1 to February 28, 2018 against an actual event "
  "range of January 3 to February 16, 2018; (iii) the stated account scope of \"user account 'mholt'\" "
  "against the 12 rows attributed to \"bthornton\" or \"SYSTEM\"; and (iv) the truncated hash and the "
  "absence of any device-level custody record for the SanDisk media. It also resolves how Meridian came to "
  "hold a document bearing opposing counsel's work-product legend, which must be settled before the extract "
  "is shown to any witness. This is a records-and-discovery question, not a legal-advice question, and "
  "should be answered from correspondence and request logs."),

 ("L-11",
  "Complaint paragraphs 97 and 109 allege that SkyVault \"first discovered the misappropriation of its trade "
  "secrets upon reviewing Meridian's PathForge white paper published in or about July 2022.\" What does "
  "Meridian know, as a matter of fact, about SkyVault's earlier awareness — including any pre-2024 "
  "communication with Meridian, and the February 2018 incident and March 5, 2018 forensic report reflected "
  "in Exhibit F?",
  "Complaint paras. 97 and 109 (identical discovery allegations in Counts IV and V), para. 51 (the event "
  "\"was flagged by SkyVault's IT administrator on February 12, 2018\"), para. 50 (Exhibit F), paras. 14-16 "
  "and 24 (DTSA and TUTSA jurisdictional and statutory framing). Exhibit F, \"Report Metadata\" cell B6 "
  "(\"Date of Report: March 5, 2018\"), cells B13-B14; \"Forensic Log\" Row # 38 (02/12/2018 escalation to "
  "HR; ticket INC-2018-00417; alert ALT-2018-0209-0041), Row # 40 (litigation hold instruction), Row # 46 "
  "(02/15/2018 exit interview note), Row # 50 (02/16/2018: \"Matter referred to legal counsel at "
  "Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP\"). Response Letter P0016 (reservation of defences including "
  "\"unenforceability\" and challenges to validity).",
  "The supplied documents contain an unresolved tension that only factual inquiry can develop. Exhibit F "
  "records, in February and March 2018, an automated alert, HR escalation, a litigation hold, a permissions "
  "audit, a completed exit interview, evidence preservation, engagement of a forensic examiner, incident "
  "closure, and referral to the same firm that filed this action — followed by a forensic report dated "
  "March 5, 2018 — while Complaint paras. 97 and 109 plead first discovery in July 2022. That bears on "
  "accrual and on the limitations period for Counts IV and V, and on the credibility of those two "
  "paragraphs. The question is confined to what Meridian factually knows and holds; any assessment of a "
  "limitations defence, and any advice about it, is privileged and must not be elicited here. Note that "
  "para. 97 and para. 109 are verbatim identical, which is itself worth confirming against SkyVault's "
  "discovery responses."),

 ("L-12",
  "Who at Meridian is the custodian of each of the following: the complete 42-page PathForge white paper and "
  "its drafting file; the March 12, 2024 letter and its delivery record; Meridian's onboarding file for Dr. "
  "Holt; the compliance materials referenced in the April 5 letter; every preservation notice issued in this "
  "matter; and the complete PathForge repository history?",
  "White Paper P0006 (excerpt disclaimer — \"an excerpt of the full PathForge Technical White Paper (42 "
  "pages) ... containing Sections 1-5 and Section 7, omitting detailed hardware specifications (Section 6) "
  "and appendices\") and the Sec. 6 placeholder. Complaint para. 61 (the March 12, 2024 letter, not "
  "supplied), para. 57 and Exhibit List entry \"Exhibit G,\" paras. 38(e), 91(e) and 105(e) (TS-5, hardware "
  "integration specifications for LiDAR sensor arrays). Response Letter P0011 (compliance processes), P0025 "
  "(cc line). Exhibit F \"Report Metadata\" cells B7-B8 and B13 (illustrating the consequence of an "
  "under-specified collection scope).",
  "Converts every gap identified in this memorandum into a named custodian and a collectable item, which is "
  "the operational output the presiding partner needs. Section 6 is singled out because it is the omitted "
  "portion of Meridian's own publication that maps most directly onto TS-5, and because the claim chart at "
  "Complaint para. 67 cites a \"Section 2.1\" and a \"Section 5.1\" that do not correspond to the excerpt's "
  "structure — resolving Question H-22 requires the complete paper and its drafting file, not further "
  "inference from a partial document. The collection scope should be specified with the precision that "
  "Exhibit F's own metadata lacks."),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Part VII
SEQUENCE = [
 ("h1", "VII.  RECOMMENDED INTERVIEW SEQUENCE"),
 ("p", "Recommended order: first, the Meridian technical team; second, Meridian's legal lead; last, Dr. "
       "Marcus Holt. This order is a recommendation, not the only defensible one, and Part VII.D below "
       "states the circumstance in which it should be varied."),
 ("h2", "A.  First — Meridian technical team"),
 ("p", "They hold the artifacts against which every other witness's account must be measured: repository "
       "and commit history, dependency and license manifests, test harnesses and raw benchmark data, build "
       "and release records. Interviewing them first means that when Holt and the legal lead speak, the "
       "interviewer already has the documentary frame and can ask targeted verification questions instead "
       "of open reconstruction, and can tell immediately whether an answer is consistent with the record."),
 ("p", "They also present the fewest procedural complications. Their knowledge is predominantly technical "
       "fact, so the interview can proceed at full depth without the privilege bifurcation Part VI requires "
       "and without the conflict-of-interest and Upjohn determinations Part III.D requires for Holt. And "
       "their material is the most perishable in the case: repository migrations, platform changes, "
       "decommissioned shares, and departed contractors degrade it irreversibly, while pleadings and letters "
       "do not degrade at all. Question T-2 exists precisely because early history may already have been "
       "lost, and it should be asked before more of it is."),
 ("p", "A third reason is that their answers determine whether the two representations already made in "
       "writing to opposing counsel have any foundation. The April 5, 2024 letter asserts independent "
       "development and \"robust internal compliance processes,\" and white paper Section 7.2 asserts that "
       "\"[a]ll PathForge technology was developed independently.\" Those are party positions, not "
       "established facts, and the technical team is the only group that can say whether artifacts exist to "
       "support them. The legal lead should not be interviewed about the basis for those statements until "
       "that is known."),
 ("h2", "B.  Second — Meridian's legal lead"),
 ("p", "By then the technical record exists, so the legal lead can be asked to match preservation scope, "
       "custodian lists, and compliance artifacts to what the engineers actually described, rather than "
       "being asked in the abstract. Question L-4 becomes a comparison exercise instead of an inventory "
       "request, and Question L-7 can be framed around a known set of artifacts."),
 ("p", "This is also the most privilege-sensitive interview, and running it second minimises risk in two "
       "ways. The interviewer already knows which protected topics are unavoidable and which can be deferred, "
       "so fewer questions need to be cut off mid-answer, and fewer half-elicited privileged narratives end "
       "up in the record. Equally, anything the engineers may have said that touches privilege can be "
       "screened before this session rather than after."),
 ("p", "Most importantly, the legal lead is the only witness positioned to act on the gaps immediately. "
       "Questions L-6, L-10 and L-12 exist so that hold notices can be issued or supplemented, the complete "
       "42-page white paper and its drafting file collected, the March 12, 2024 letter and its delivery "
       "record located, Holt's onboarding file retrieved, the 12,797 unselected Exhibit F events requested, "
       "and the handling question about SkyVault's work-product legend resolved — all before Holt is "
       "interviewed. Sequencing the legal lead last would forfeit that, because the material he can obtain "
       "is exactly the material the Holt interview needs in order to be productive."),
 ("h2", "C.  Last — Dr. Marcus Holt"),
 ("p", "Holt carries the greatest personal exposure of any witness in the package. He is named as the actor "
       "in Complaint paragraphs 94 and 107, Count VII is pleaded on his own contractual obligations at "
       "paragraphs 127 through 132, Prayer paragraph 5 seeks judgment that \"Meridian, through Holt, has "
       "breached\" the ECIAA, and ECIAA Section 8.3 exposes him to the prevailing party's fees — while "
       "Meridian's liability is framed as derivative at paragraph 130. Their interests may therefore "
       "diverge. The conflict question at L-9 and the determinations at Part III.D must be resolved before "
       "he is interviewed, and that cannot properly be improvised at the start of a session."),
 ("p", "Substantively, he is the witness most likely to have absorbed the published narrative. His name and "
       "title appear on the white paper cover page at P0003, and its provenance statements at Section 7.2 "
       "are the assertions SkyVault is attacking. Interviewing him first risks setting the frame that "
       "everyone else then conforms to, and risks taking his account of 2018 before anyone has checked "
       "whether a commit history, a dependency manifest, or a test log confirms it. Interviewing him last "
       "means his account can be tested against the repository record, the compliance artifacts, the "
       "complete 42-page paper, and the Exhibit F discrepancies — and that variances can be explored while "
       "he is still in the room."),
 ("p", "He is also the only witness who can authenticate or contradict the 38 \"mholt\" rows in Exhibit F, "
       "resolve the February 8 or February 9 timing question created by the extract's own Event Date and "
       "Event Time (CT) columns at Rows # 33 through # 35, account for the 3,174 files and 8,791.2 MB by "
       "which Row # 34 exceeds the six logged staging exports at Rows # 27 through # 32, and say what "
       "became of the SanDisk device. Those are precise questions. They are far more productive once the "
       "surrounding record is assembled, and far more likely to produce a usable answer if put after the "
       "technical and legal interviews have narrowed what is actually in dispute."),
 ("h2", "D.  When this order should be varied, and how the sequence cross-validates"),
 ("p", "Interviewing Holt first would be preferable only on a specific showing: a concrete risk that his "
       "recollection or his devices will degrade, or a need for an early admission or denial to shape "
       "preservation. If such a risk emerges from the technical interviews — for example, if Question T-9 "
       "or H-7 locates the USB drive or personal repositories that need immediate securing — a short, "
       "narrowly scoped preservation-only contact with Holt should be moved ahead of the full interview, "
       "with the conflict assessment handled first and the substantive questions deferred. A second "
       "variation is available where the matter team needs the legal lead's collection authority before any "
       "engineer can be interviewed effectively, in which case L-6, L-10 and L-12 alone can be taken early "
       "as a short records-only session, with the remainder of Part VI left in second position."),
 ("p", "The sequence is iterative rather than linear, and its value lies in the cross-validation loop. The "
       "technical interviews generate document requests and identify which artifacts exist; the legal lead's "
       "collection narrows the Holt agenda to the questions the artifacts cannot answer; and Holt's answers "
       "generate a second round of technical verification, because a claim about 2018 that the commit "
       "history does not support must be put back to the module owners. Two hard dependencies govern the "
       "loop. First, no question put to any witness may attribute content to the March 12, 2024 letter "
       "beyond Complaint paragraph 61 and the April 5, 2024 response. Second, no witness should be shown "
       "Exhibit F until the interviewer has confirmed how Meridian came to hold a file bearing SkyVault's "
       "attorney-work-product legend at \"Report Metadata\" cell B14, since that affects handling, "
       "admissibility argument, and any later challenge to the extract."),
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Appendix A
APPENDIX = [
 ("h1", "APPENDIX A — CONSOLIDATED COLLECTION AND CONFIRMATION LIST"),
 ("p", "Each item below is a gap identified in Part II.F or created by a question above. No item is assumed "
       "to exist or not to exist; each is to be requested, and the absence of a response recorded."),
 ("h2", "From SkyVault (through discovery or a records request)"),
 ("bullet", "The complete Confluence and endpoint event population of 12,847 events referenced at Exhibit F \"Report Metadata\" cell B13, together with the selection criteria used to derive the 50 rows produced. Supports H-6, L-10."),
 ("bullet", "A file-level manifest of the 4,700 files recorded at Exhibit F \"Forensic Log\" Row # 34, with per-file paths and hashes, and any verification against the destination \"F:\\SkyVault_Export\\\". Supports H-6, H-7, T-4, L-10."),
 ("bullet", "The forensic image of workstation SV-ENG-WS-014 and the Hargrove Forensics Group findings, plus the untruncated SHA-256 hash and the complete custody record for locker HFG-2018-0034 and for the SanDisk Ultra 128GB device \"USB\\VID_0781&PID_5581\\4C530001221029118035\". Supports H-7, L-10."),
 ("bullet", "Incident ticket INC-2018-00417 and alert ALT-2018-0209-0041 in full, including all attachments and the HR escalation file. Supports H-4, H-5, L-11."),
 ("bullet", "The February 15, 2018 exit-interview record for Holt and any written certification requested or received under ECIAA Sec. 3.5(c). Supports H-4, L-5."),
 ("bullet", "Holt's SkyVault personnel file, project assignments, and any written invention disclosures made under ECIAA Sec. 5.1. Supports H-1, H-11."),
 ("bullet", "Any AeroCore firmware source, and any instance of navfusion.c, pathoptengine.h, or swarm_proto.cpp; plus records of access to any SkyVault source-code repository by the \"mholt\" account, which \"Report Metadata\" cell B8 confirms was outside the reviewed data sources. Supports H-2, H-3, T-4."),
 ("bullet", "Complaint Exhibits A, B, C and D (the '561, '227 and '889 patents and Copyright Registration No. TX 9-142-338), and Exhibit G as filed in complete form. Supports H-13, H-22, T-6, L-12."),
 ("bullet", "Records bearing on SkyVault's awareness before July 2022, including any communication with Meridian between March 5, 2018 and March 12, 2024. Supports L-8, L-11."),
 ("h2", "From Meridian (internal collection, privileged review first)"),
 ("bullet", "The complete 42-page PathForge White Paper v1.0 (July 2022), including Section 6 and all appendices, and its drafting, review, and approval file. Supports H-21, H-22, H-23, T-11, L-12."),
 ("bullet", "Complete PathForge repository history for all four modules named at White Paper Sec. 7.1, including earliest commits, migration records, and any squash, rewrite, or force-push. Supports H-18, T-2, T-10, L-12."),
 ("bullet", "Dependency manifests, license texts, NOTICE and attribution files, vendored directories, and any open-source review or bill-of-materials output. Supports T-3, H-17, H-27, L-4."),
 ("bullet", "Test harnesses, raw flight-test data, benchmark methodology documents, and the source data behind every figure in White Paper Secs. 3.3, 4.4 and 5.4. Supports H-19, T-5, T-11."),
 ("bullet", "Build, release, version, and customer-deployment records from April 2018 forward, and the records supporting the September 2020 v1.0 launch, the Q1 2021 swarm deployment, and the Q3 2021 dashboard release. Supports H-16, H-19, H-20, T-1, T-5."),
 ("bullet", "Product records locating the three features pleaded at Complaint para. 68 — the configurable threat parameter interface, multi-resolution environmental mapping, and the fail-safe return-to-home function. Supports T-6, H-22."),
 ("bullet", "Holt's Meridian onboarding file, including any IP questionnaire, prior-restriction attestation, or clean-room instruction, and Meridian's written IP and compliance policies with their training and attestation outputs. Supports T-7, T-8, L-4, L-5."),
 ("bullet", "All preservation notices issued in this matter, custodian lists, hold acknowledgments, and auto-deletion suspension records, with dates. Supports H-31, L-6, T-9, L-12."),
 ("bullet", "Any internal provenance, similarity, or code-comparison analysis ever run on PathForge, with its instruction chain and distribution list. Supports T-4, L-7."),
 ("bullet", "The March 12, 2024 letter and its delivery record, all Meridian-SkyVault correspondence from March 12, 2024 to October 2, 2024, and the file transmitted to Brackwell & Haines before the April 5, 2024 response. Supports L-2, L-3, L-8, L-12."),
 ("bullet", "Meridian's founder, employee, contractor, and advisor roster from April 2018 forward, screened for prior SkyVault affiliation. Supports H-14, T-7, L-5."),
 ("h2", "From public or third-party sources"),
 ("bullet", "The DroneNav repository at github.com/dronenav/dronenav, archived as of August 15, 2017 and as of each relevant later date, with its license file and full commit history. Supports H-25, H-26, H-27, T-3."),
 ("bullet", "The RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit at github.com/mholt-robotics/robonav-cal, with its MIT license, commit history, and any evidence of reuse. Supports H-9, H-10, T-3, T-4."),
 ("bullet", "Holt's Georgia Institute of Technology doctoral dissertation and associated 2014-2015 research artifacts on autonomous ground vehicle path planning. Supports H-9, H-12, T-10."),
 ("bullet", "The four works cited at White Paper References items 1-4 (Vasquez 2016; DroneNav 2017; Nakamura and Okonkwo 2015; Ferreira et al. 2016), and any Meridian records of their review. Supports H-28, T-3."),
 ("bullet", "Public posting dates, distribution lists, and third-party archive captures of the PathForge white paper. Supports H-24, L-11."),
]
",
  "file_path": "/tmp/build_memo_part3.py"
}

{
  "content": "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Render the witness-interview outline memorandum to /app/output/result.docx."""
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp')
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_LINE_SPACING, WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

from build_memo_part1 import MEMO_HEADER, S1
from build_memo_part2 import HOLT_INTRO, HOLT
from build_memo_part3 import TECH_INTRO, TECH, LEGAL_INTRO, LEGAL, SEQUENCE, APPENDIX

FONT = "Times New Roman"
OUT = "/app/output/result.docx"

doc = Document()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- page setup
for sec in doc.sections:
    sec.top_margin = Inches(1.0)
    sec.bottom_margin = Inches(1.0)
    sec.left_margin = Inches(1.0)
    sec.right_margin = Inches(1.0)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- base styles
st = doc.styles['Normal']
st.font.name = FONT
st.font.size = Pt(11)
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), FONT)
pf = st.paragraph_format
pf.space_after = Pt(8)
pf.space_before = Pt(0)
pf.line_spacing_rule = WD_LINE_SPACING.SINGLE

def _mkstyle(name, size, bold=False, italic=False, caps=False,
             before=14, after=6, color=None, base='Normal'):
    s = doc.styles.add_style(name, 1)  # WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH
    s.base_style = doc.styles[base]
    s.font.name = FONT
    s.font.size = Pt(size)
    s.bold = bold
    s.italic = italic
    if color:
        s.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(*color)
    s.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), FONT)
    if caps:
        c = OxmlElement('w:caps'); c.set(qn('w:val'), '1')
        s.element.rPr.append(c)
    s.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    s.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    s.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return s

H1 = _mkstyle('MemoH1', 12, bold=True, caps=True, before=20, after=8)
H2 = _mkstyle('MemoH2', 11, bold=True, before=14, after=6)
H3 = _mkstyle('MemoH3', 11, bold=True, italic=True, before=12, after=4)
QST = _mkstyle('MemoQ', 11, before=10, after=3)
QST.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
QST.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
QST.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.4)
ANN = _mkstyle('MemoAnn', 10, before=0, after=3)
ANN.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
ANN.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = False
BUL = _mkstyle('MemoBul', 11, before=0, after=5)
BUL.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.45)
BUL.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def add_field(par, instr):
    r = par.add_run()
    fc = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fc.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    it = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); it.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); it.text = instr
    fc2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fc2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'separate')
    t = OxmlElement('w:t'); t.text = "1"
    fc3 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fc3.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    r._r.append(fc); r._r.append(it); r._r.append(fc2); r._r.append(t); r._r.append(fc3)
    return r

def hrule(par, sz=6, color="000000"):
    pPr = par._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement('w:pBdr')
    bottom = OxmlElement('w:bottom')
    bottom.set(qn('w:val'), 'single'); bottom.set(qn('w:sz'), str(sz))
    bottom.set(qn('w:space'), '1'); bottom.set(qn('w:color'), color)
    pbdr.append(bottom); pPr.append(pbdr)

def para(text, style=None, align=None, indent=None, after=None, bold=False,
         italic=False, size=None, before=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic
    if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    if indent is not None: p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(indent)
    if after is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    return p

def body(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def bullet(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='MemoBul')
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    r0 = p.add_run("\u2022\t")
    p.add_run(text)
    return p

def question(label, text, source, purpose):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='MemoQ')
    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
    r = p.add_run(label + ".\t")
    r.bold = True
    p.add_run("\u201c" + text + "\u201d")
    for tag, val in (("Source: ", source), ("Evidentiary purpose: ", purpose)):
        a = doc.add_paragraph(style='MemoAnn')
        a.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
        rt = a.add_run(tag); rt.bold = True
        a.add_run(val)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

def render_block(kind, payload):
    if kind == 'h1':
        para(payload, style='MemoH1')
    elif kind == 'h2':
        para(payload, style='MemoH2')
    elif kind == 'h3':
        para(payload, style='MemoH3')
    elif kind == 'p':
        body(payload)
    elif kind == 'bullet':
        bullet(payload)
    elif kind == 'num':
        p = doc.add_paragraph(style='MemoBul')
        p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.JUSTIFY
        p.add_run("(" + str(render_block.counter) + ")\t")
        p.add_run(payload)
        render_block.counter += 1
render_block.counter = 1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- header/footer
hdr = doc.sections[0].header
hp = hdr.paragraphs[0]
hp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
hr = hp.add_run("PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL \u2014 ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION \u2014 "
                "ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT \u2014 PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION")
hr.bold = True; hr.font.size = Pt(8); hr.font.name = FONT
hrule(hp, sz=4)

ftr = doc.sections[0].footer
fp = ftr.paragraphs[0]
fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
fr = fp.add_run("SkyVault Technologies LLC v. Meridian Dynamics, Inc., No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG "
                "\u2014 Witness Interview Outline Memorandum  |  Page ")
fr.font.size = Pt(8); fr.font.name = FONT
add_field(fp, " PAGE ")
fr2 = fp.add_run(" of ")
fr2.font.size = Pt(8); fr2.font.name = FONT
add_field(fp, " NUMPAGES ")
for r in fp.runs:
    r.font.size = Pt(8); r.font.name = FONT

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- title block
t = doc.add_paragraph()
t.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
t.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
rt = t.add_run("MEMORANDUM")
rt.bold = True; rt.font.size = Pt(16); rt.font.name = FONT
rt.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0, 0, 0)

t2 = doc.add_paragraph()
t2.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
t2.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(10)
rt2 = t2.add_run("Witness Interview Outline and Preparation Memorandum")
rt2.bold = True; rt2.font.size = Pt(12); rt2.font.name = FONT

pv = doc.add_paragraph()
pv.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
pv.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(12)
rpv = pv.add_run(MEMO_HEADER["priv"])
rpv.bold = True; rpv.font.size = Pt(9); rpv.font.name = FONT
hrule(pv, sz=12)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- header table
labels = [("TO:", MEMO_HEADER["to"]), ("FROM:", MEMO_HEADER["from"]),
          ("DATE:", MEMO_HEADER["date"]), ("RE:", MEMO_HEADER["re"])]
tbl = doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
tbl.autofit = False
for lab, val in labels:
    row = tbl.add_row()
    c0, c1 = row.cells
    c0.width = Inches(0.85); c1.width = Inches(5.65)
    p0 = c0.paragraphs[0]; p0.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    r0 = p0.add_run(lab); r0.bold = True; r0.font.size = Pt(10.5); r0.font.name = FONT
    p1 = c1.paragraphs[0]; p1.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
    p1.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.LEFT
    r1 = p1.add_run(val); r1.font.size = Pt(10.5); r1.font.name = FONT
    if lab == "RE:":
        r1.bold = True

sp = doc.add_paragraph(); sp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
hrule(sp, sz=12)
sp2 = doc.add_paragraph(); sp2.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- document body
for kind, payload in S1:
    render_block(kind, payload)

for kind, payload in HOLT_INTRO:
    render_block(kind, payload)
for item in HOLT:
    if len(item) == 2:
        render_block(item[0], item[1])
    else:
        question(*item)

for kind, payload in TECH_INTRO:
    render_block(kind, payload)
for item in TECH:
    question(*item)

for kind, payload in LEGAL_INTRO:
    render_block(kind, payload)
for item in LEGAL:
    question(*item)

for kind, payload in SEQUENCE:
    render_block(kind, payload)

for kind, payload in APPENDIX:
    render_block(kind, payload)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- closing
para("END OF MEMORANDUM", style='MemoH2')
body("This memorandum is an interview-design document prepared for the internal use of the matter team. "
     "It states no conclusion on the merits of any claim or defence, adopts no allegation in the complaint "
     "as fact, and treats no position taken in Meridian's April 5, 2024 response letter or in the July 2022 "
     "PathForge white paper as established. Every factual proposition in it is traceable to one of the five "
     "supplied materials and is cited to the paragraph, section, worksheet, row, cell, event, or record "
     "identifier from which it is drawn. It is privileged and confidential attorney work product prepared in "
     "anticipation of litigation and should not be distributed outside the matter team.")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- properties
cp = doc.core_properties
cp.title = ("Witness Interview Outline and Preparation Memorandum — "
            "SkyVault Technologies LLC v. Meridian Dynamics, Inc., No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG")
cp.subject = "Privileged internal fact investigation — interview design"
cp.author = "IP Litigation Group — Internal Fact Investigation Team"
cp.category = "Attorney Work Product"
cp.comments = ("PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT. "
               "Interview outline memorandum covering Dr. Marcus Holt, the Meridian technical team, and "
               "Meridian's legal lead.")
cp.keywords = "privileged; work product; witness interview; SkyVault; Meridian; PathForge; ECIAA; Exhibit F"

os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)
doc.save(OUT)
print("saved:", OUT, os.path.getsize(OUT), "bytes")

# ---- self-check
d2 = Document(OUT)
n_par = len(d2.paragraphs)
n_tab = len(d2.tables)
words = sum(len(p.text.split()) for p in d2.paragraphs)
qs = [p.text for p in d2.paragraphs if p.text.strip()[:1] in 'HTL' and '.\t' in p.text[:8]]
src = sum(1 for p in d2.paragraphs if p.text.startswith('Source:'))
pur = sum(1 for p in d2.paragraphs if p.text.startswith('Evidentiary purpose:'))
print(f"paragraphs={n_par} tables={n_tab} words={words}")
print(f"questions={len(qs)} Source annotations={src} Evidentiary purpose annotations={pur}")
assert src == pur == len(qs), "annotation count mismatch"
import re
ids = [p.text.split('.')[0] for p in qs]
print("question ids:", " ".join(ids))
",
  "file_path": "/tmp/build_memo.py"
}

{
  "content": "# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""QA verification of /app/output/result.docx"""
from docx import Document
import re, zipfile, os

P = '/app/output/result.docx'
print("exists:", os.path.exists(P), "size:", os.path.getsize(P), "bytes")
print("valid zip / docx parts:", sorted(n for n in zipfile.ZipFile(P).namelist())[:8])

d = Document(P)
paras = [p.text for p in d.paragraphs]
full = "\n".join(paras)
words = len(full.split())
print(f"\nparagraphs={len(paras)}  tables={len(d.tables)}  words={words}")

# --- question / annotation integrity
qs = [p for p in paras if re.match(r'^[HTL]-\d+\.\t', p)]
src = [p for p in paras if p.startswith('Source:')]
pur = [p for p in paras if p.startswith('Evidentiary purpose:')]
ids = [p.split('.')[0] for p in qs]
print(f"\nquestions={len(qs)}  Source={len(src)}  Purpose={len(pur)}")
print("ids:", " ".join(ids))
exp = [f"H-{i}" for i in range(1,32)] + [f"T-{i}" for i in range(1,12)] + [f"L-{i}" for i in range(1,13)]
print("id sequence complete & ordered:", ids == exp)
print("counts match:", len(qs) == len(src) == len(pur) == 54)

# --- every question is followed by its two annotations, in order
idx = {p:i for i,p in enumerate(paras) if p in qs}
ok = True
for q in qs:
    i = paras.index(q)
    nxt = [paras[j] for j in range(i+1, min(i+4, len(paras))) if paras[j].strip()]
    if not (nxt[0].startswith('Source:') and nxt[1].startswith('Evidentiary purpose:')):
        ok = False; print("  ANNOTATION ORDER FAIL:", q[:40], [n[:20] for n in nxt[:2]])
print("annotation order correct for all questions:", ok)

# --- required structural elements
need = {
  "Three witness sections": ["WITNESS GROUP A", "WITNESS GROUP B", "WITNESS GROUP C"],
  "Six lead families": ["Lead family 1", "Lead family 2", "Lead family 3",
                        "Lead family 4", "Lead family 5", "Lead family 6"],
  "Sequence part": ["RECOMMENDED INTERVIEW SEQUENCE", "First —", "Second —", "Last —"],
  "Core sections": ["PURPOSE, SCOPE, AND LIMITS", "MATERIALS REVIEWED", "INTERVIEW CONVENTIONS",
                    "CONSOLIDATED COLLECTION"],
}
for k, vs in need.items():
    miss = [v for v in vs if v not in full]
    print(f"{k}: {'OK' if not miss else 'MISSING '+str(miss)}")

# --- all five source files cited by name
files = ["skyvault-complaint.docx","exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx","holt-eciaa-agreement.docx",
         "pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx","meridian-cd-response.docx"]
print("\nfile names cited in memo:", {f: full.count(f) for f in files})

# --- citation-density check on the Source annotations
srcblob = " ".join(src)
for pat, lbl in [(r'para\.?\s*\d+', 'Complaint para'), (r'Sec\.\s*\d', 'ECIAA Sec'),
                 (r'Exhibit A', 'ECIAA Exhibit A'), (r'Row #\s*\d+', 'Exhibit F Row #'),
                 (r'"Report Metadata"|Report Metadata', 'Report Metadata sheet'),
                 (r'cell B\d+', 'metadata cell'), (r'Sec\.\s*\d\.\d', 'White Paper Sec x.y'),
                 (r'\bUTC\b', 'UTC timestamp'), (r'\bCT\b', 'Central time'),
                 (r'P00\d\d', 'response letter para')]:
    print(f"  {lbl:<22} hits={len(re.findall(pat, srcblob))}")

# --- the four key quantitative findings must appear
print("\nkey findings present:")
for s in ["12,847", "4,700", "3,174", "8,791.2", "1,526", "9,682.0", "18,473.2",
          "(02/08 CT)", "Sensor Integration Layer", "Threat Assessment Module",
          "Dynamic Path Replanner", "Flight Controller API", "mholt-robotics/robonav-cal",
          "github.com/dronenav/dronenav", "INC-2018-00417", "ALT-2018-0209-0041",
          "HFG-2018-0034", "SV-ENG-WS-014", "4C530001221029118035",
          "Jordan Kessler", "March 12, 2024", "TX 9-142-338", "2:24-cv-00817-JRG",
          "42 pages", "Section 6"]:
    print(f"   {'OK ' if s in full else 'MISS'}  {s}")

# --- discipline checks: no overreach language, no non-English
bad = ["it is established that", "this proves that Meridian", "we will win",
       "Meridian is liable", "Holt misappropriated the", "infringement is clear"]
print("\noverreach phrases:", {b: full.lower().count(b) for b in bad})
nonascii = sorted(set(ch for ch in full if ord(ch) > 127))
print("non-ascii chars used:", nonascii)
cjk = [ch for ch in nonascii if '\u4e00' <= ch <= '\u9fff']
print("CJK characters present (must be empty):", cjk)

# --- no leftover placeholders / broken concatenation
print("\nplaceholder scan:", {t: full.count(t) for t in ["TODO","XXX","TBD","Lorem","{{","}}"," None ","nan"]})
print("double-space-in-sentence artifacts:", len(re.findall(r'[a-z]  [a-z]', full)))
print("\nheading inventory:")
for p in d.paragraphs:
    if p.style.name.startswith('MemoH'):
        print(f"   [{p.style.name}] {p.text}")
",
  "file_path": "/tmp/qa.py"
}
