rubric.criterion: The Holt section locates the ECIAA disclosure of the RoboNav sensor-calibration tool.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分明确定位了该披露：H-9 与 H-10 均引用“holt-eciaa-agreement.docx, ECIAA Exhibit A Table Row 2”，并写明“RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit (open-source)”、2015 年、MIT License 及 GitHub 地址。

rubric.criterion: The Holt prior-work questions ask for content, origin, contributors, pre-SkyVault records, and relationship to PathForge without presuming overlap.
rubric.reason: H-9要求说明两项既有工作的内容、开发时间与方式、贡献者及现存文档；H-10进一步询问RoboNav与PathForge具体模块的关系，并以“Did any part…? If so”开放询问而未预设重合。相关问题还明确要求调取博士论文、RoboNav提交历史及PathForge仓库记录进行验证。

rubric.criterion: The PathForge development questions locate the whitepaper's stated development-start timing.
rubric.reason: PathForge 开发问题明确定位了白皮书所述的开发起点。例如 H-15、H-18 和 T-10 均引用 pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx 第 7.2 节的“April 2018…PathForge development begins”，并同时引用第 1 节“Developed from the ground up beginning in 2018”。

rubric.criterion: The PathForge development-start questions seek early requirements, repositories, architecture materials, testing records, and personnel.
rubric.reason: PathForge 开发起点问题覆盖了所要求的内容：H-15 询问最初参与人员、最早书面或绘制材料及首个版本能力；H-18 询问最早设计文档、代码库、分支、提交、原型和测试台；H-19 询问测试活动、基准方法和底层记录；T-2、T-5、T-10 进一步核实早期仓库历史、测试记录及成立前后的设计与人员情况。

rubric.criterion: The Meridian technical-team section locates the whitepaper's DroneNav public-project reference.
rubric.reason: Meridian technical-team section expressly locates the DroneNav reference in pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx, including White Paper §§ 2, 4.2, and 7.2 and References item 2, identifying the GitHub repository, URL, and first-commit date of August 15, 2017 (notably in T-3 and related technical-team questions).

rubric.criterion: The Holt section locates the whitepaper authorship and title information for Holt.
rubric.reason: Holt 部分设有“White paper title, authorship, review, and publication”专题；H-21 询问各节作者及 Holt 的个人贡献，并将作者署名定位到白皮书封面 P0003（“Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder / PathForge Engineering Team”）。该部分也明确识别为 July 2022 PathForge white paper，全文前部给出完整标题“PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation”。

rubric.criterion: The answer treats the whitepaper authorship and title information only as a lead for role, drafting, review, approval, or technical-information-supply questions.
rubric.reason: 虽然后文明确称封面署名只是 publication credit，并设置 H-21、H-23、T-11 等问题核实撰写、审阅和批准，但 Holt 章节开头仍直接断言其“is the cover-page author”，将署名信息表述为既定作者身份，而不只是访谈线索，因此不满足“only as a lead”。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section locates the counsel response made on behalf of Meridian and its officers and directors to SkyVault's demand letter.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分虽定位了2024年4月5日律师回函及其与3月12日来函的关系，但仅表述律师代表“Meridian Dynamics, Inc.”，未说明或定位该回函亦系代表Meridian的高管和董事作出。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead questions use the counsel response to probe receipt, escalation, investigation, response authority, and materials reviewed.
rubric.reason: 法律负责人问题以4月5日律师回函为线索，分别询问来函的接收与内部流转（L-2）、法律团队职责及参与人员/权限（L-1）、回函前开展的事实调查和向外部律师提供的材料与人员（L-3）、内部审查或比对工作（L-7），并明确追问回函中独立开发、专利审查及合规表述所依据的文件。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section locates the response's visible cc line identifying Jordan Kessler as Meridian VP of Legal.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分明确指出并定位了回函中的抄送行：L-1 的 Source 引用“meridian-cd-response.docx, Response Letter P0025 (cc line: 'Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc. (via email)')”。

rubric.criterion: The Jordan Kessler questions seek his role in receiving, reviewing, approving, or coordinating the response without assuming final authority.
rubric.reason: L-1先确认Kessler的职务、任期及责任范围；L-2询问来函的接收、流转和处理；L-3询问4月5日回函前由谁收集并向外部律师提供了哪些材料。问题旨在查明其接收、审阅准备和协调回函的实际角色，未预设其拥有最终批准权。

rubric.criterion: The response uses open-ended wording for matters that can only be confirmed through interviews.
rubric.reason: 产出对需证人确认的事实普遍采用开放式问法，如“Please describe...”“Walk me through...”“What became of...”“Who wrote...”及“Take me through...”，并明确要求证人说明人物、时间、过程、来源及文件位置，而非预设事实或要求简单认可结论。

rubric.criterion: The response identifies missing records as interview-confirmation or document-request topics rather than confirmed facts.
rubric.reason: 产出明确将缺失材料作为待确认或调取事项，而非既定事实。例如 Part II.F 写明“Each is converted below into an interview confirmation or a collection request, and none is treated as established”，并在各问题及 Appendix A 中将代码库、人员档案、完整取证数据、保全记录、完整白皮书等列为需向证人确认或请求收集的材料。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum provides questions that can actually be asked orally of the designated witnesses, rather than only topic headings, document lists or statements of desired findings.
rubric.reason: 备忘录为三类指定证人分别提供了大量可直接口头询问的完整问题，例如 H-1“Please describe your role...”、T-1“Which PathForge modules have you personally worked on...”、L-2“Describe how the March 12, 2024 letter reached Meridian...”。这些并非仅有主题标题、文件清单或预期结论。

rubric.criterion: The memo stays within the provided source universe and uses missing documents only as confirmation or production topics.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确限定题包事实来源为五份指定材料，并反复区分诉状主张、当事方立场及材料实际证明范围。未提供的完整取证日志、代码库、人事档案、3月12日来函、完整白皮书等均被表述为待证人确认或调取的事项，未被当作已证实事实。

rubric.criterion: The memo assigns witness topics to the witness category best positioned to answer them.
rubric.reason: 备忘录按证人知识范围合理分工：Holt负责其任职、访问、既有工作及个人行为；技术团队负责PathForge模块、代码来源、依赖、测试和发布记录；法务负责人负责诉前函件、保全、合规流程及特权边界，均由最适合掌握相应事实的证人类别回答。

rubric.criterion: The memo does not upgrade a limited interview-preparation record into a full infringement, provenance, preservation, or merits conclusion.
rubric.reason: 备忘录反复明确其仅为访谈设计文件，并将诉状、回函、白皮书、ECIAA及Exhibit F分别限定为主张、当事方立场、公开陈述、合同记录和选定日志摘录。其明确声明不构成侵权比对、独立开发意见、完整保全结论或实体胜诉判断，并把代码来源、技术相似性、文件接收、保全完整性等未决事项转化为访谈及调取问题，未作最终侵权、来源、保全或实体结论。

rubric.criterion: The answer states an evidence gap or unconfirmed point as a definite conclusion.
rubric.reason: 存在将未确认事项写成确定结论的表述。例如，备忘录称 Exhibit F 的 50 行“therefore an advocacy selection”，但材料仅表明这些事件被选为与委托范围相关，不能直接证明其为“倡导性”筛选；又称该摘录“It does not reach source code at all”，而已知范围仅能证明未纳入源代码管理系统，不能排除 Confluence 等已审查来源中存在代码文件，且文中后来还列出 .py 文件下载事件。

rubric.criterion: No non-empty, readable Microsoft Word (.docx) memorandum containing substantive, scorable text is submitted, including where the required file is missing, empty, corrupted, in the wrong file format, or wholly unreadable.
rubric.reason: modelResponse 明确包含正式交付物“result.docx”，且展示了大量非空、可读、实质性的英文法律备忘录内容；不存在文件缺失、空白、格式错误、损坏或完全不可读的情形。

rubric.criterion: The response is severely redundant, repeatedly restating the same facts, questions, sources, purposes, or cautions without adding a distinct interview function, thereby materially impairing the memorandum’s concision and usability.
rubric.reason: 备忘录篇幅极度膨胀并反复重述相同内容，已明显影响可用性。例如 Exhibit F 的“50/12,847 条选定事件”、USB 时间差异、3,174 个文件差额及工作成果标记在材料评述、多个 H/T/L 问题、访谈顺序和附录中多次完整展开；“独立开发及合规仅为当事方立场”、缺失材料不得视为事实、特权边界等警示也被反复复述。附录又大幅重复各问题已列的调取事项，许多 Evidentiary purpose 反复说明同一证明限制，未增加独立访谈功能，严重削弱简洁性与现场使用效率。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum identifies Exhibit F as a 50-event selected extract from a stated 12,847-event review population for account mholt and limits it to SkyVault-side access, export, device, and response leads rather than treating it as a complete forensic record or proof of Meridian receipt or PathForge use.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确指出 Exhibit F 是针对“mholt”账户、从 12,847 条事件中筛选出的 50 条事件摘录，并反复说明其仅涵盖 SkyVault 侧的 Confluence、终端安全、AD 和 USB 记录，不是完整取证总体。其还明确否认该摘录能够证明 Meridian 收到材料或 PathForge 使用了材料，并将这些事项转化为访谈与调取问题。

rubric.criterion: The Holt interview reconciles the bulk removable-media event's 2018-02-09 02:18 UTC timestamp with its displayed February 8, 8:18 p.m. Central local time, or otherwise uses the timestamp without creating a false chronology.
rubric.reason: H-6明确同时引用Row #34的UTC时间“2018-02-09T02:18:12Z”和Central显示时间“08:18:12 PM (02/08 CT)”，并将日期差异作为需Holt解释的访谈事项；H-7及访谈顺序部分亦延续该核对，未制造错误时间线。

rubric.criterion: Across its questions and annotations, the memorandum independently distinguishes pleaded allegations, the final counsel response's advocacy statements, the public White Paper's later marketing/technical assertions, operative ECIAA terms and disclosures, and logged forensic events, and does not use one source type as automatic proof of a different proposition.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确且持续区分各材料的证明范围：将诉状称为 SkyVault 的指控，将 2024 年回函中的否认、独立开发及合规陈述视为当事方立场，将白皮书视为 2022 年公开营销/技术陈述，将 ECIAA 作为合同条款及既有发明披露，并将 Exhibit F 限定为 SkyVault 侧选取的日志事件摘录。各问题及注释反复说明这些来源不能自动证明误用、侵权、独立开发、技术来源或完整保全，并在多来源问题中分别交代各来源支持的不同命题。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum recognizes that the complaint lists patents, a copyright registration, the ECIAA, Exhibit F and the White Paper, while the supplied universe does not include the patents, registration, full March 12 letter, source code, or a technical comparison, and therefore treats those missing materials as collection or confirmation needs rather than silently supplying their contents.
rubric.reason: 备忘录明确区分了诉状所列材料与实际题包：Part II.F 指出专利附件 A-C、版权登记附件 D、完整的 2024 年 3 月 12 日来函、AeroCore 源代码及技术比对均未提供；并在相关问题及 Appendix A 中将其转化为调取、保全或证人确认事项，而未擅自补充其内容。同时也识别了已提供的 ECIAA、Exhibit F 和白皮书及其证明范围。

rubric.criterion: The Holt section connects the February 15 exit-interview/device note to ECIAA return, deletion, certification, and exit obligations, while asking Holt to confirm what occurred and avoiding treatment of the SkyVault administrator note as conclusive proof of breach.
rubric.reason: H-4 将 Exhibit F Row #46 的 2018年2月15日退出访谈及未归还/识别 USB 设备的管理员记录，与 ECIAA 第3.5(a)-(c)节的返还、删除和书面认证义务及第4.4节的退出访谈义务明确关联，并开放式询问 Holt 实际发生了什么。备忘录同时明确该记录只是“IT administrator's second-hand notes”而非访谈记录或违约证明，未将其视为决定性证据。

rubric.criterion: The Holt section addresses the January 24 view and/or February 8 bulk export from the Business/CustomerData space and seeks purpose, authorization, content and corroboration, using the log's 'outside normal Engineering scope' note as a lead rather than a legal conclusion.
rubric.reason: H-6涵盖2月8日的批量导出（包括Row #32），询问转移内容/经过、目的、去向及是否获授权或有人知情，并要求以书面批准等记录核验；H-29又明确引用Rows #17、#32的Business/CustomerData访问及“outside normal Engineering scope”注释，同时指出该注释只是SkyVault管理员的表述，且与诉状所称Holt因客户演示和提案工作而有访问权限存在张力，要求进一步核实而非作法律结论。

rubric.criterion: The Holt questions distinguish the ECIAA's Confidential Information definition and invention-assignment provisions from its general-skills/public-information allowance and Exhibit A prior-invention disclosure, and seek records capable of applying those boundaries to later PathForge work.
rubric.reason: Holt 问题明确区分了不同合同边界：H-8 引用 ECIAA 第 2.4、3.1、3.5 条调查 SkyVault 材料及保密义务；H-9 至 H-11 分别围绕 Exhibit A 的两项既有发明及第 5.1—5.3 条发明披露、转让和排除规则；H-12 又明确引用第 3.4 条的一般技能、经验及公开信息保留权。问题同时要求调取书面发明披露、博士研究和 RoboNav 提交历史、PathForge 仓库与模块历史、早期设计文件等，以便将这些界限适用于后续 PathForge 工作。

rubric.criterion: The prior-work inquiry seeks contemporaneous substantiation for the disclosed Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm and RoboNav toolkit—such as dissertation, repository, contributor, release-date and license records—and does not confuse RoboNav with the White Paper's separate DroneNav reference.
rubric.reason: 备忘录对两项既有工作均要求同时代佐证：H-9询问开发时间、贡献者、后续去向及现存文档，并要求调取Georgia Tech论文记录和RoboNav提交历史；H-10进一步询问RoboNav在PathForge中的使用及来源记录，明确其2015年MIT许可、GitHub仓库和提交历史。附录还分别调取论文研究材料及RoboNav仓库、MIT许可证、提交历史和复用证据。文中始终将RoboNav与白皮书所引DroneNav作为不同项目处理，未混淆二者。

rubric.criterion: The technical-team questions seek a module-specific provenance chain for sensor fusion, GPS-denied navigation and swarm coordination, connecting contributors and source-code/repository history, including dependencies or their non-use, to both testing and release records and the records or custodians needed to verify those links. Shared questions expressly applied to each component, including a combined Navigation Module with distinguishable sensor-fusion and GPS-denied work, qualify; questions about record absence or dependency non-use are valid, without supplying invented record contents.
rubric.reason: 技术团队问题形成了符合标准的模块化来源链：T-1按模块确认贡献者及工作期间，T-2追查最早提交、分支合并和仓库迁移，T-3核查依赖及许可证记录，T-5连接构建、测试、基准和发布记录，T-9/T-11进一步确认记录位置与保管人。问题明确区分Navigation Module中的sensor fusion与GPS-denied navigation，并单列swarm coordination，且将第三方依赖、未使用情形及验证所需记录作为待确认事项，没有虚构记录内容。

rubric.criterion: The technical-team questions seek underlying test plans, raw results, approvals, drafts or source records for material White Paper performance and independent-development statements instead of treating the published figures or marketing conclusion as contemporaneous provenance proof.
rubric.reason: 技术团队问题明确要求底层材料而非采信白皮书结论：T-5询问测试工具、飞行测试、基准方法及原始结果存放位置；T-11要求每项图表和章节的源文件或数据、完整草稿及审阅人员。备忘录还反复将白皮书性能数字和“独立开发”表述界定为待验证的公开营销陈述，而非同期来源证明。

rubric.criterion: The public-source questions separately investigate DroneNav and the cited academic works by Vasquez, Nakamura and Okonkwo, and Ferreira, seeking corroborating records that distinguish awareness, citation and evaluation from modification, use or non-use. The inquiry also distinguishes cloning and dependency introduction for software sources, while academic influences can be traced through design decisions and citations; naming sources alone is insufficient.
rubric.reason: 产出对公开来源进行了分层调查。H-25至H-27分别追问对 DroneNav 的知悉、引用、下载/克隆、评估/基准测试、依赖引入、修改、成品使用及未使用，并要求许可证、提交历史、clone/fetch 日志、依赖清单和归属记录等佐证；H-28则单独调查 Vasquez、Nakamura and Okonkwo、Ferreira 等学术文献，区分阅读、引用、评估、据其实现和未使用，并要求注释论文、阅读清单、设计评审材料等记录。T-3等问题还从技术团队角度交叉核验第三方依赖、许可证和设计影响，符合该标准。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section tests the non-privileged factual basis for the response's denials, independent-development assertion and compliance-process assertion, identifies records or custodians reviewed and gaps, and does not treat the sent response as proof that those assertions are true.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分通过 L-3、L-4、L-7 等问题核查回函中否认、独立开发及“robust internal compliance processes”表述的非特权事实基础，要求说明收集和传送了哪些材料、由谁收集，并定位政策、培训记录、证明、代码扫描和审查产物及其保管人。该部分明确限定不得询问法律建议或立场形成理由，并反复说明回函仅属当事方立场、其事实表述需要文件基础，未将已发送的回函当作相关断言真实的证明。

rubric.criterion: The pre-suit-response questions limit statements about the unprovided March 12 letter to what Complaint paragraph 61 and the April 5 response actually record, while separately investigating receipt, escalation, response scope, authority and transmission.
rubric.reason: 产出明确限定未提供的 2024 年 3 月 12 日来函内容只能依据诉状第 61 段及 4 月 5 日回函，并在 L-2、L-3、L-8 等问题中分别调查收件方式与日期、内部流转/升级、回函前收集和传递给外部律师的材料、回函所涉范围及后续沟通；但对“authority”仅通过法律负责人职责及参与人员作间接确认，整体仍符合该标准。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead section asks for Meridian's actual 2024 preservation dates, custodians, systems, actions and non-privileged completion records, and does not confuse those facts with the 2018 SkyVault-side litigation-hold, imaging and access-revocation entries in Exhibit F or assume preservation was complete.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分的 L-6 明确询问 Meridian 在 2024 年 3 月 12 日来函及 10 月 2 日起诉后的实际保全日期、通知发出人和对象、所收集内容；L-12 及附录进一步要求确认保全通知、custodian lists、hold acknowledgments、系统自动删除暂停记录和相关保管人。文中明确将 Exhibit F 的 2018 年 litigation hold、工作站成像和证据保管描述为 SkyVault 侧行为，并指出“Meridian's corresponding record is absent”，未将两者混同，也未假定 Meridian 的保全完整。

rubric.criterion: The legal-lead questions seek discoverable facts, dates, actors, custodians, actions and pre-existing business records while expressly reserving legal advice, attorney communications, strategy and mental impressions for privilege/work-product review and proposing a workable screening boundary.
rubric.reason: 法务负责人部分明确划分可发现事实与受保护内容：要求询问收件日期、人员、传递路径、保全措施、托管人、既有政策及所收集材料，同时明确不询问法律意见、律师沟通内容、诉讼策略或律师思维。L-3、L-7、L-8等问题还设置了可执行的筛查边界，如仅询问“what was gathered and transmitted”及沟通的存在、日期和参与者，并规定一旦回答涉及律师建议或结论即记录主题并停止追问。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum converts identified proof gaps into targeted collection requests that name relevant systems, record types, custodians, date ranges or modules and explain how each target will test access, provenance, public-source use, preservation or the response chain; a generic request for all documents is insufficient.
rubric.reason: 备忘录将证明缺口转化为高度具体的调取请求，并明确系统、记录类型、时间范围、模块或保管人及其证明用途。例如要求调取 Exhibit F 所称 12,847 条完整事件、Row #34 的 4,700 个文件清单及哈希、SV-ENG-WS-014 镜像和 SanDisk 设备保管链；按四个 PathForge 模块调取完整仓库与提交历史、依赖和许可证清单、测试原始数据及发布记录；由法律负责人确认完整白皮书、Holt 入职档案、保全通知、3 月 12 日来函及后续通信的保管人。各请求还分别说明用于检验访问、技术来源、DroneNav 等公开来源使用、保全完整性或诉前回函链，并非笼统要求“所有文件”。

rubric.criterion: The memorandum ends with a brief recommendation identifying first, second and last witness categories and explaining why that order is workable in light of privilege scope, available records, witness knowledge and the value of using earlier interviews or collection to test later accounts. A professionally supported legal-first, technical-first, Holt-first or staged hybrid order qualifies without matching a prescribed sequence.
rubric.reason: 备忘录在第 VII 部分明确给出顺序：第一为 Meridian technical team，第二为 Meridian's legal lead，最后为 Dr. Marcus Holt；并说明技术记录最易灭失且可先建立代码、依赖、测试与发布的客观框架，法务随后处理保全、调取与特权边界，最后以已收集记录和前序访谈交叉检验 Holt 的说法，同时考虑其个人风险、Upjohn 与独立律师问题。还提出必要时提前进行记录型法务访谈或针对 Holt 的保全型接触，符合可执行且非唯一顺序的要求。

rubric.criterion: The proposed sequence and actual questions form a coherent cross-witness verification plan: a record, custodian or factual account sought from an earlier witness category is used in planned later questioning to confirm, challenge, explain or refine another category’s account, while preserving what each source can and cannot establish. One connected chain or conditional follow-up plan qualifies; repeated topics without a downstream testing relationship do not.

For a question relying on multiple materials, each source’s contribution is identifiable from the question and annotations rather than a collective list of filenames; one annotation block can cover coherent related follow-ups with an unambiguous mapping.

MEMORANDUM

Witness Interview Outline and Preparation Memorandum

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT — PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION

TO:

Presiding Partner, IP Litigation Group; Meridian Dynamics, Inc. Matter Team

FROM:

IP Litigation Group — Internal Fact Investigation Team

DATE:

September 20, 2026

RE:

SkyVault Technologies LLC v. Meridian Dynamics, Inc., No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG (E.D. Tex., Marshall Division) — Witness Interview Outline and Preparation Memorandum (Dr. Marcus Holt; Meridian Technical Team; Meridian Legal Lead)





I.  PURPOSE, SCOPE, AND LIMITS OF THIS MEMORANDUM

This memorandum is an interview-design document. Its purpose is to tell the matter team what to ask three categories of witness, why each question matters, and which of the five supplied materials supplies the factual lead behind each question. It is prepared at the request of the presiding partner in connection with a privileged internal fact investigation of the allegations SkyVault Technologies LLC has asserted against Meridian Dynamics, Inc.

This memorandum is not, and must not be treated as, testimony, a declaration, a pleading, an infringement or claim chart, a non-infringement opinion, a settlement communication, an independent-development opinion, or a prediction of outcome on the merits. No question below assumes that any allegation in the complaint is true, and no question assumes that any position Meridian has taken is true. Where the supplied materials state a contested proposition, the proposition is treated below as a lead to be developed, not as a fact to be recited.

Only the five materials listed in Part II have been used as sources of in-package fact. Where a question depends on personnel files, source-code repositories, development records, preservation records, internal communications, compliance materials, the complete forensic population, or any technical comparison, that dependency is expressed as an interview confirmation or a document-collection request. Nothing of that kind is assumed to exist, and nothing of that kind is treated here as established.

One limitation is stated expressly because it constrains several questions below. The March 12, 2024 cease-and-desist letter from Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP to Meridian was not supplied. Its contents are known to us only through Complaint paragraph 61 and through the matters that Meridian's April 5, 2024 response addresses. Nothing in this memorandum attributes to that letter any content, tone, deadline, enclosures, or demand beyond those two sources, and interviewers must observe the same limit.

A.  Structure of this memorandum

Part II assesses each supplied material and states what it can and cannot prove; it also lists the material that is missing. Part III states the drafting conventions used for every question. Parts IV, V, and VI contain the three witness sections. Part VII gives a recommended interview sequence with reasons. Appendix A consolidates the collection requests generated by the questions, so that each identified gap is tied to a named item and a custodian.

B.  Coverage of the required lead families

Six lead families are carried through the questions below, and each appears in more than one witness section so that the accounts can be cross-checked:

•Holt's employment and access history — Questions H-1 through H-8; corroborated at T-7, T-8, L-5.

•Holt's disclosed prior work — Questions H-9 through H-14 (ECIAA Exhibit A); corroborated at T-3, T-4, L-5.

•PathForge development origins — Questions H-15 through H-20; corroborated at T-1, T-2, T-5, T-10.

•White paper title and authorship information — Questions H-21 through H-24; corroborated at T-6, T-11, L-12.

•DroneNav and other public sources — Questions H-25 through H-29; corroborated at T-3, T-4, L-4, L-7.

•Pre-suit correspondence chain — Questions H-30, H-31, L-2, L-3, L-6, L-8, L-10, L-11; corroborated at T-9.

II.  MATERIALS REVIEWED AND THEIR ACTUAL EVIDENTIARY REACH

Each of the five supplied materials proves a different and narrower thing than the use to which an adversary would put it. The assessments below govern how every question in Parts IV through VI is framed. Interviewers should read this Part before conducting any interview.

A.  skyvault-complaint.docx — a pleading, and therefore SkyVault's assertions

Plaintiff's Original Complaint, dated October 2, 2024, filed in the Eastern District of Texas, Marshall Division, as Civil Action No. 2:24-cv-00817-JRG, with 151 numbered allegations, nine counts, a prayer for relief, a jury demand, a certificate of service, and an exhibit list.

What it establishes: what SkyVault alleges, which patents and registrations it asserts, what it demands, and when it says it acted. Paragraph 61 is our only in-package description of the March 12, 2024 letter. Paragraph 62 and the April 5 response fix the pre-suit exchange.

What it does not establish: misappropriation, infringement, access, copying, willfulness, damages, or SkyVault's ownership or validity positions. The great majority of the operative factual allegations are expressly qualified — see paragraphs 2, 12, 49, 54, 55, 59, 60, 69, 78, 86, 94, 95, 107, 108, 119, 120, 130, and 146, each pleaded "on information and belief." The claim chart at paragraph 67 is one party's mapping of claim language onto a marketing document; it is not a technical finding, and paragraph 67 itself introduces it "[b]y way of example and without limitation." Exhibits A through D are listed but not supplied, and Exhibit G is supplied only in part.

B.  meridian-cd-response.docx — Meridian's own party position, made through counsel

Letter dated April 5, 2024 from Laura Brackwell, Partner, Brackwell & Haines LLP, Austin, Texas, to Theresa N. Voss, Partner, Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP, Dallas, Texas, sent "Via Email and U.S. Certified Mail," cc to Jordan Kessler, VP of Legal, Meridian Dynamics, Inc.

What it establishes: what Meridian said to SkyVault's counsel on April 5, 2024, and which demands it declined — cessation of manufacture, use, sale and distribution; the $15 million licensing fee; and access to source-code repositories for forensic audit. It also records a reservation of non-infringement, invalidity, unenforceability, and independent-development defenses, an offer of without-prejudice discussions, and a request that SkyVault refrain from contacting Meridian's officers and employees directly.

What it does not establish: the truth of any statement it makes. The letter says of itself that it is written "without waiver of any rights, claims, or defenses" and that "[n]othing in this letter constitutes an admission of any fact, allegation, liability, or wrongdoing of any kind." Its denials, its statement that "Meridian independently developed its PathForge platform through the efforts of its engineering teams," and its statement that "Meridian maintains robust internal compliance processes designed to safeguard against the unauthorized use of third-party intellectual property" are representations, not proof of independent development, not proof that compliance processes exist, and not proof that no third-party material entered PathForge. Each is an affirmative factual assertion already made in writing to opposing counsel, and each therefore requires a documentary foundation before it is repeated. That requirement drives the sequencing recommendation in Part VII.

C.  pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx — a 2022 public technical and marketing statement

"PathForge: Next-Generation Autonomous Navigation," PathForge White Paper v1.0, July 2022, cover-attributed to "Dr. Marcus Holt, CTO and Co-Founder / PathForge Engineering Team / Meridian Dynamics, Inc.," classified on its face as "Public Release / Marketing Technical Paper," and expressly "an excerpt of the full PathForge Technical White Paper (42 pages)" containing "Sections 1-5 and Section 7, omitting detailed hardware specifications (Section 6) and appendices."

What it establishes: that Meridian published these statements in July 2022, and what it said. Its prior-art narrative — the Vasquez (2016) paper, the DroneNav open-source project first committed August 15, 2017, Nakamura and Okonkwo (2015), and Ferreira et al. (2016) — is Meridian's own public characterization of PathForge's foundations, and is usable against SkyVault's secrecy position to that extent.

What it does not establish: that PathForge was in fact developed from the ground up or independently. Statements such as "Developed from the ground up beginning in 2018" (Section 1) and "All PathForge technology was developed independently by the Meridian engineering team" (Section 7.2) are self-serving published assertions by the party now accused; they are potential party admissions if untrue, not evidence of truth. The benchmark tables in Sections 3.3, 4.4 and 5.4 are unverified published figures. The cover attribution is a publication credit, not a verified statement of who wrote what. And because the excerpt is partial, the absence of a term from it proves nothing about the complete paper — a point of direct consequence for Question H-22.

D.  holt-eciaa-agreement.docx — a contract and a prior-invention disclosure

Employee Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement between SkyVault Technologies LLC and Dr. Marcus Holt, effective and dated June 13, 2016, comprising recitals, Sections 1 through 10, a signature page executed by Dr. Rajan Mehta for SkyVault and by Dr. Marcus Holt, and Exhibit A (Prior Inventions Disclosure), initialed "_M.H._" and dated June 13, 2016.

What it establishes: the parties, the effective date, the position and reporting line (Section 1.1), the defined terms (Section 2), the confidentiality and return-of-materials obligations (Sections 3.1-3.5, including the Section 3.5(c) duty to "certify in writing"), the residual-skills preservation (Section 3.4), the systems and removable-media rules (Sections 4.1-4.2), the invention-disclosure, assignment, exclusion, and work-made-for-hire framework (Sections 5.1-5.4), the twelve-month non-solicitation period (Section 7.1), the remedies and Texas forum provisions (Sections 8-9), and the two Prior Inventions listed on Exhibit A — an "Autonomous Ground Vehicle Path Planning Algorithm" (2014-2015, Georgia Institute of Technology doctoral research, no patent filed) and the "RoboNav Sensor Calibration Toolkit (open-source)" (2015, MIT License, github.com/mholt-robotics/robonav-cal).

What it does not establish: that any obligation was breached; that any invention was conceived or reduced to practice during employment; that the Exhibit A items were or were not used at Meridian; that Holt did or did not return materials or deliver a Section 3.5(c) certification; or anything about conduct after June 13, 2016. Exhibit A is a snapshot of pre-employment work as of that date, and it is silent on everything after it. Note also that the agreement is silent as to whether the listed items were ever actually used, and that its existence does not make its Exhibit A a complete inventory of Holt's pre-2016 work.

E.  exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx — a SkyVault-side selected extract

"SkyVault Technologies LLC — Confluence Workspace IT Forensic Log Extract," designated "Exhibit F" in this action, prepared by Hargrove Forensics Group for Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP, report dated March 5, 2018, forensic examiner Thomas R. Hargrove, CFCE, EnCE, and marked "CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT / PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION." Two visible worksheets: "Report Metadata" (cells A1:B14) and "Forensic Log" (cells A1:U51, header row 1, 50 event rows, freeze pane at A2, autofilter A1:U51).

What it establishes: what SkyVault's own systems logged against the account "mholt" and what its administrators wrote in the incident record. It is a party-commissioned vendor product, not a neutral or court-appointed finding.

What it does not establish, and five features of the extract that must be put to witnesses rather than assumed:

(1)It is not the population. "Report Metadata" cell B13 states that the extract "contains selected events relevant to the bulk file transfer incident involving user mholt on 02/09/2018" and that the "[f]ull audit log contains 12,847 events for the review period; 50 events selected as relevant to the scope of engagement." Cell B9 states "Total Events in Scope: 50." The 50 rows are therefore an advocacy selection of roughly 0.4 percent of the population, and no inference about what did not happen can be drawn from them.

(2)It is not a file-level manifest. "Forensic Log" Row # 34, the headline BULK_COPY_TO_REMOVABLE event, records a File/Object Name of "[Multiple — see File Count]" and a File Count of 4,700 with a Total Size of 18,473.2 MB. No list of the 4,700 files, no per-file hashes, and no verification against the destination appears anywhere in the extract. The assertion in Complaint paragraphs 49, 94, 107 and 129 that the download included all five trade-secret categories TS-1 through TS-5 rests on the Confluence space names in the Row # 34 Notes field, not on any identified file.

(3)Its own date and time columns disagree about the headline event. Row # 34 (worksheet row 35) carries Timestamp (UTC) "2018-02-09T02:18:12Z," Event Date "02/09/2018," and Event Time (CT) "08:18:12 PM (02/08 CT)." The same pattern appears at Row # 33 (worksheet row 34; USB_DEVICE_CONNECTED, "08:17:44 PM (02/08 CT)") and Row # 35 (worksheet row 36; USB_DEVICE_DISCONNECTED, "09:42:58 PM (02/08 CT)"). On the extract's own Central-time column the entire USB episode occurred on the evening of February 8, 2018, while Complaint paragraphs 48, 50, 94, 107 and 128(a) all plead February 9, 2018. Other rows convert without discrepancy — Row # 32 (worksheet row 33; "2018-02-08T22:44:06Z" to "04:44:06 PM") and Rows # 36-37 (worksheet rows 37-38) — so the annotation appears deliberate and the Event Date column appears keyed to the UTC date. Throughout this memorandum, Exhibit F events are cited by the "Row #" column value with the worksheet row given in parentheses where precision matters; because the header occupies worksheet row 1, the worksheet row is always the "Row #" value plus one.

(4)The staged transfers do not account for the headline transfer. Rows # 27 through # 32 record six BULK_EXPORT events between February 2 and February 8, 2018 from Confluence to "Local Disk (C:\Users\mholt\Downloads\export_MMDDYY)": 347 files / 1,842.6 MB (/Engineering/SensorFusion/Archives/); 218 / 1,105.3 (/Engineering/FlightPath/); 189 / 924.7 (/Engineering/SwarmProtocol/); 276 / 2,214.8 (/Engineering/HardwareIntegration/); 412 / 3,127.4 (/Engineering/SensorFusion/); and 84 / 467.2 (/Business/CustomerData/). Those six rows total 1,526 files and 9,682.0 MB. Row # 34 records 4,700 files and 18,473.2 MB reaching the USB device. Within the 50 selected rows, 3,174 files and 8,791.2 MB — roughly 68 percent of the file count and 48 percent of the volume — are unaccounted for.

(5)It does not reach source code at all. "Report Metadata" cell B7 limits the Scope of Review to "All Confluence workspace and endpoint security events for user account 'mholt' ... during the period January 1, 2018 through February 28, 2018," and cell B8 lists the Data Sources as "SkyVault Confluence Server v6.12.2 audit logs; Endpoint Security Agent (v4.1) event logs; Active Directory authentication logs; USB device connection registry." No source-code management system is within scope. Consistently with that, no row among Rows # 1 through # 50 mentions AeroCore, navfusion.c, pathoptengine.h, swarm_proto.cpp, or any version-control system — the very files named in Complaint paragraphs 33, 116 and 118. The actual event dates also run only from January 3 to February 16, 2018, not through February 28; and although the stated scope is the "mholt" account, 12 of the 50 rows are attributed to "bthornton" (8 rows) or "SYSTEM" (4 rows). The "Reviewed By" and "Review Date" columns are populated for only 10 of the 50 rows and are blank for every one of the 38 "mholt" rows.

Two further features bear on handling and on cross-examination. First, cell B12 records chain of custody as "Server image acquired 02/19/2018 by T. Hargrove; verified hash SHA-256: 9a3f...d82e; stored in evidence locker HFG-2018-0034" — a truncated hash, for a server image, with no device-level custody record for the SanDisk media identified at Rows # 33-35 by the identifier "USB\VID_0781&PID_5581\4C530001221029118035 (SanDisk Ultra 128GB)." Second, the file bears SkyVault's attorney-work-product legend at cell B14 yet was filed as a public complaint exhibit; the matter team should confirm how Meridian came to hold it before it is shown to any witness, since that affects both handling and any later challenge.

Finally, the extract contains a timing tension with the pleading that no supplied document resolves. Rows # 38 through # 50 record, between February 12 and February 16, 2018, an automated alert (reference ALT-2018-0209-0041), escalation to HR under incident ticket INC-2018-00417, a litigation hold instruction, a permissions audit, access revocations, a requested forensic image, a completed exit interview, evidence storage of workstation SV-ENG-WS-014, closure of the incident ticket, and a note that the "[m]atter [was] referred to legal counsel at Callister, Voss & Greenbaum LLP" — the same firm that filed this action — followed by a forensic report dated March 5, 2018. Complaint paragraphs 97 and 109 nonetheless allege that "SkyVault first discovered the misappropriation of its trade secrets upon reviewing Meridian's PathForge white paper published in or about July 2022." Whether that allegation can be reconciled with SkyVault's own 2018 incident record is a factual question for discovery and for Question L-11. It is identified here as a tension in the supplied documents, not as a conclusion about accrual or limitations.

F.  Material not supplied, and how each gap is handled

The following are not in the package. Each is converted below into an interview confirmation or a collection request, and none is treated as established in either direction:

•The March 12, 2024 Callister, Voss & Greenbaum cease-and-desist letter (Complaint para. 61; response letter Re line).

•Complaint Exhibits A, B, C (the '561, '227 and '889 patents), Exhibit D (Copyright Registration No. TX 9-142-338), and the complete Exhibit G — specifically white paper Section 6 and the appendices.

•The 12,797 unselected Confluence and endpoint events referenced at "Report Metadata" cell B13, and any file-level manifest of the 4,700 files at Row # 34.

•SkyVault's personnel file for Holt, any Section 5.1 written invention disclosures, the exit-interview record, any Section 3.5(c) written certification, incident ticket INC-2018-00417, alert ALT-2018-0209-0041, the SV-ENG-WS-014 forensic image and the examiner's findings, and the USB device itself.

•Any AeroCore firmware, and any instance of navfusion.c, pathoptengine.h, or swarm_proto.cpp.

•Meridian's PathForge repositories and full commit history, dependency and license manifests, open-source review records, build and release records, test harnesses and raw test data, and customer deployment records.

•Meridian's onboarding file for Holt, its IP and compliance policies and their outputs, its preservation notices and custodian lists, and any internal provenance or similarity analysis.

•The DroneNav repository (github.com/dronenav/dronenav), its license, and any Meridian clone, fork, or evaluation record; the RoboNav repository (github.com/mholt-robotics/robonav-cal) and Holt's Georgia Tech dissertation.

•Any Meridian-SkyVault correspondence after April 5, 2024 and before the October 2, 2024 filing.

III.  INTERVIEW CONVENTIONS

A.  Annotation format

Every question below is followed by two annotations. "Source:" names the file supplying the lead and, where the material permits, locates the lead within it — by complaint paragraph, agreement section or subsection, Exhibit A table row, white paper section, subsection, cover paragraph or table, worksheet name, "Row #" column value, worksheet row number, cell reference, event date, event time and time zone, event type, source system, file or object name, device identifier, ticket or alert reference, or record ID. Where a question rests on more than one material, the annotation states separately which proposition each source supports and marks the distinction with a dash clause; file names are never merely listed. On its first citation of a given material, each annotation gives the file name in full and establishes the short form used thereafter within that annotation.

The short forms used throughout, and the files they denote, are: "Complaint para. n" for skyvault-complaint.docx; "ECIAA Sec. n," "ECIAA Recitals," and "ECIAA Exhibit A" for holt-eciaa-agreement.docx; "White Paper Sec. n," "White Paper P00nn" (cover and front-matter paragraphs), and "White Paper References item n" for pathforge-whitepaper-excerpt.docx; "Response Letter para. n" (body paragraphs), "Response Letter item n" (the three numbered refusals), and "Response Letter P00nn" (letterhead, Re line, signature block, and cc line) for meridian-cd-response.docx; and "Exhibit F" for exhibit-f-forensic-log.xlsx, cited by worksheet ("Report Metadata" or "Forensic Log"), "Row #" column value, worksheet row number, and cell. "Evidentiary purpose:" states what the answer is for — which allegation, defence, element, or collection decision it advances — and, where relevant, what the answer cannot establish.

B.  Open-ended phrasing

Questions that seek a fact the witness must supply are framed openly — "describe," "walk me through," "what became of," "who," "when" — and do not embed the answer. Questions that test a document put the document to the witness and ask for confirmation or correction rather than asking the witness to adopt it. No question below asks a witness to agree that SkyVault's information was misappropriated, that PathForge was independently developed, that preservation was complete, that any license was obtained, or that any technology came from any particular source. Where a distinction matters, the question enumerates the alternatives so the witness must choose among them — see Question H-26, which separates awareness, citation, evaluation, cloning, dependency incorporation, modification, shipped use, and non-use.

C.  Privilege and work-product handling

The legal-lead questions in Part VI are deliberately bifurcated. Facts that are ordinarily discoverable — dates of receipt, routing, distribution lists, hold notices, custodian identities, what was gathered and transmitted, which policies exist and what they produced — are asked directly. Communications seeking or conveying legal advice, counsel's mental impressions, assessments of the strength of SkyVault's claims, the reasoning behind the positions taken in the April 5, 2024 letter, and the substance of any settlement discussion are not asked, and if a witness volunteers them the interviewer should note the topic, stop, and log it rather than develop it. Question L-3 states this boundary on the face of the question so the record shows the limit was observed.

D.  Preliminary matter for the Holt interview

Before Dr. Holt is interviewed, two threshold determinations must be made and documented: whether an Upjohn-type warning is required and in what terms, and whether his interests diverge from Meridian's such that he should be advised to retain separate counsel. The reason is on the face of the pleading. Holt is named personally as the actor in Complaint paragraphs 94 and 107 and Count VII is pleaded on his contractual obligations at paragraphs 127 through 132, while Meridian's liability is framed as derivative at paragraph 130 and Prayer paragraph 5 seeks a judgment that "Meridian, through Holt, has breached" the ECIAA. Question L-9 develops the factual state of representation and communication so that this determination can be made on information rather than assumption. It is a reason to interview Holt last, not a reason to avoid him.

V.  WITNESS GROUP B — MERIDIAN TECHNICAL TEAM

The technical-team witnesses are the only source in this matter that can convert PathForge's published self-description into a module-by-module, contributor-by-contributor, artifact-by-artifact record, and their materials — repositories and commit history, dependency and license manifests, test harnesses and raw test data, build and release records — will either substantiate or undercut the independent-development position stated in Meridian's April 5, 2024 letter and in white paper Section 7.2. Because the white paper attributes the work collectively to "the PathForge Engineering Team" and to "a dedicated engineering team of approximately 45 working full-time on PathForge development and customer integration," individual testimony is required to establish who actually did what, and which engineers can speak to the April 2018 through September 2020 period at all.

This group should be interviewed after Holt's first session and before the legal lead, for the reasons given in Part VII: their knowledge is predominantly technical fact, so the interview can proceed at full depth without the privilege bifurcation Part VI requires and without the conflict-of-interest assessment Part III.D requires for Holt; and their artifacts are the most perishable material in the case, since repository migrations, decommissioned shares, and departed contractors permanently degrade them.

Interview format: one session per witness, sequenced so that module owners for the four modules named in white paper Section 7.1 are covered first, followed by release and test engineering, then infrastructure and DevOps custodians, then whoever owns build and open-source compliance. A further caution: this witness is both a fact witness and a likely privilege holder, and the interview record may itself become the subject of a privilege dispute. The session should be documented as fact-gathering, questions should be phrased to elicit events rather than assessments, and the interviewer should record contemporaneously where a protected topic was reached and declined so that the boundary is visible on the face of the record.

VII.  RECOMMENDED INTERVIEW SEQUENCE

Recommended order: first, the Meridian technical team; second, Meridian's legal lead; last, Dr. Marcus Holt. This order is a recommendation, not the only defensible one, and Part VII.D below states the circumstance in which it should be varied.

A.  First — Meridian technical team

They hold the artifacts against which every other witness's account must be measured: repository and commit history, dependency and license manifests, test harnesses and raw benchmark data, build and release records. Interviewing them first means that when Holt and the legal lead speak, the interviewer already has the documentary frame and can ask targeted verification questions instead of open reconstruction, and can tell immediately whether an answer is consistent with the record.

They also present the fewest procedural complications. Their knowledge is predominantly technical fact, so the interview can proceed at full depth without the privilege bifurcation Part VI requires and without the conflict-of-interest and Upjohn determinations Part III.D requires for Holt. And their material is the most perishable in the case: repository migrations, platform changes, decommissioned shares, and departed contractors degrade it irreversibly, while pleadings and letters do not degrade at all. Question T-2 exists precisely because early history may already have been lost, and it should be asked before more of it is.

A third reason is that their answers determine whether the two representations already made in writing to opposing counsel have any foundation. The April 5, 2024 letter asserts independent development and "robust internal compliance processes," and white paper Section 7.2 asserts that "[a]ll PathForge technology was developed independently." Those are party positions, not established facts, and the technical team is the only group that can say whether artifacts exist to support them. The legal lead should not be interviewed about the basis for those statements until that is known.

B.  Second — Meridian's legal lead

By then the technical record exists, so the legal lead can be asked to match preservation scope, custodian lists, and compliance artifacts to what the engineers actually described, rather than being asked in the abstract. Question L-4 becomes a comparison exercise instead of an inventory request, and Question L-7 can be framed around a known set of artifacts.

This is also the most privilege-sensitive interview, and running it second minimises risk in two ways. The interviewer already knows which protected topics are unavoidable and which can be deferred, so fewer questions need to be cut off mid-answer, and fewer half-elicited privileged narratives end up in the record. Equally, anything the engineers may have said that touches privilege can be screened before this session rather than after.

Most importantly, the legal lead is the only witness positioned to act on the gaps immediately. Questions L-6, L-10 and L-12 exist so that hold notices can be issued or supplemented, the complete 42-page white paper and its drafting file collected, the March 12, 2024 letter and its delivery record located, Holt's onboarding file retrieved, the 12,797 unselected Exhibit F events requested, and the handling question about SkyVault's work-product legend resolved — all before Holt is interviewed. Sequencing the legal lead last would forfeit that, because the material he can obtain is exactly the material the Holt interview needs in order to be productive.

C.  Last — Dr. Marcus Holt

Holt carries the greatest personal exposure of any witness in the package. He is named as the actor in Complaint paragraphs 94 and 107, Count VII is pleaded on his own contractual obligations at paragraphs 127 through 132, Prayer paragraph 5 seeks judgment that "Meridian, through Holt, has breached" the ECIAA, and ECIAA Section 8.3 exposes him to the prevailing party's fees — while Meridian's liability is framed as derivative at paragraph 130. Their interests may therefore diverge. The conflict question at L-9 and the determinations at Part III.D must be resolved before he is interviewed, and that cannot properly be improvised at the start of a session.

Substantively, he is the witness most likely to have absorbed the published narrative. His name and title appear on the white paper cover page at P0003, and its provenance statements at Section 7.2 are the assertions SkyVault is attacking. Interviewing him first risks setting the frame that everyone else then conforms to, and risks taking his account of 2018 before anyone has checked whether a commit history, a dependency manifest, or a test log confirms it. Interviewing him last means his account can be tested against the repository record, the compliance artifacts, the complete 42-page paper, and the Exhibit F discrepancies — and that variances can be explored while he is still in the room.

He is also the only witness who can authenticate or contradict the 38 "mholt" rows in Exhibit F, resolve the February 8 or February 9 timing question created by the extract's own Event Date and Event Time (CT) columns at Rows # 33 through # 35, account for the 3,174 files and 8,791.2 MB by which Row # 34 exceeds the six logged staging exports at Rows # 27 through # 32, and say what became of the SanDisk device. Those are precise questions. They are far more productive once the surrounding record is assembled, and far more likely to produce a usable answer if put after the technical and legal interviews have narrowed what is actually in dispute.

D.  When this order should be varied, and how the sequence cross-validates

Interviewing Holt first would be preferable only on a specific showing: a concrete risk that his recollection or his devices will degrade, or a need for an early admission or denial to shape preservation. If such a risk emerges from the technical interviews — for example, if Question T-9 or H-7 locates the USB drive or personal repositories that need immediate securing — a short, narrowly scoped preservation-only contact with Holt should be moved ahead of the full interview, with the conflict assessment handled first and the substantive questions deferred. A second variation is available where the matter team needs the legal lead's collection authority before any engineer can be interviewed effectively, in which case L-6, L-10 and L-12 alone can be taken early as a short records-only session, with the remainder of Part VI left in second position.

The sequence is iterative rather than linear, and its value lies in the cross-validation loop. The technical interviews generate document requests and identify which artifacts exist; the legal lead's collection narrows the Holt agenda to the questions the artifacts cannot answer; and Holt's answers generate a second round of technical verification, because a claim about 2018 that the commit history does not support must be put back to the module owners. Two hard dependencies govern the loop. First, no question put to any witness may attribute content to the March 12, 2024 letter beyond Complaint paragraph 61 and the April 5, 2024 response. Second, no witness should be shown Exhibit F until the interviewer has confirmed how Meridian came to hold a file bearing SkyVault's attorney-work-product legend at "Report Metadata" cell B14, since that affects handling, admissibility argument, and any later challenge to the extract.

END OF MEMORANDUM

This memorandum is an interview-design document prepared for the internal use of the matter team. It states no conclusion on the merits of any claim or defence, adopts no allegation in the complaint as fact, and treats no position taken in Meridian's April 5, 2024 response letter or in the July 2022 PathForge white paper as established. Every factual proposition in it is traceable to one of the five supplied materials and is cited to the paragraph, section, worksheet, row, cell, event, or record identifier from which it is drawn. It is privileged and confidential attorney work product prepared in anticipation of litigation and should not be distributed outside the matter team.
